        self.dims = dims

    def embed_texts(self, texts: Sequence[str], *, batch_size: int = 0, **kwargs: Any) -> List[List[float]]:
        return [[float((hash(t) >> i) & 1) for i in range(self.dims)] for t in texts]


mgr.register_custom_generator(name="hash", generator=HashEmbeddings(dims=16))

BaseEmbeddingsGenerator.__init__ takes keyword-only model, session_id and logger.

docs.title: Using Embeddings with a Vector Database
docs.text:
Generators plug directly into the vector database add-on (agent_addons.embeddings_store.EmbeddingsSDK) as the embedder:

from agent_addons.embeddings_store import EmbeddingsSDK

vdb = EmbeddingsSDK(provider="weaviate", weaviate_url="http://localhost:8080")
vdb.insert_texts("KnowledgeBase", ["hello world"], embedder=mgr.get_generator("openai"))

See Accessing Vector Databases.

docs.title: Graph Database Integration — Client Developer Documentation
Introduction
docs.text:
The Graph Database add-on gives agents access to ArangoDB, a multi-model (document + graph) database, through the ArangoSDK class in the agent_addons package.

ArangoSDK wraps python-arango and adds:

  • AQL queries with bind variables.
  • Database and collection lifecycle management, including edge collections for graphs.
  • Document CRUD and batched insert/upsert.
  • Bulk ingestion from Python iterables, local JSON/JSONL files, or S3 objects.
  • Admin helpers for server status, role, cluster health and arbitrary admin endpoints.

Typical workflow:

  1. Declare an AddonItem in the Subject Specification to record the graph database connection (optional).
  2. Create an ArangoSDK client in your agent.
  3. Create collections, write documents and edges, and query with AQL.
  4. Optionally bulk-ingest data from files or S3.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
ArangoSDK is part of agent_addons (libs/agents-addons), which installs python-arango, requests and boto3.

pip install ./libs/agents-addons

docs.title: Registering Graph DB in Subject Specification
docs.text: Graph databases can be recorded in the subject's integrations.addons list using AddonItem.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Any

@dataclass
class AddonItem:
    addon_id: str
    addon_type: str
    addon_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "addon_id": "graphs-primary",
  "addon_type": "graph_db",
  "addon_config": {
    "endpoint": "http://arangodb.default.svc.cluster.local:8529",
    "db_name": "knowledge",
    "username": "root",
    "password": "secret"
  }
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text:
Field Type Description addon_id str Unique identifier for this add-on. addon_type str Add-on kind, e.g. "graph_db". addon_config Dict[str, Any] Connection settings. Use the ArangoSDK constructor arguments as keys (see below).

The agents SDK does not create clients from add-on entries automatically. Read the entry from self.subject.integrations.addons in your agent and build the client yourself:

from agent_addons.graph import ArangoSDK

class MyAgent:
    def __init__(self, subject, context):
        self.subject = subject
        self.context = context
        addon = next(a for a in subject.integrations.addons if a.addon_type == "graph_db")
        self.graph = ArangoSDK(**addon.addon_config)

docs.title: Import and Setup
docs.text:
from agent_addons.graph import ArangoSDK

graph = ArangoSDK(
    endpoint="http://localhost:8529",
    db_name="knowledge",
    username="root",
    password="secret",
)
Argument Default Description endpoint — (required) ArangoDB URL (trailing / is removed) db_name "_system" Database to open username None Username (used together with password) password None Password jwt_token None JWT for authentication (sent as Authorization: Bearer ...) verify_ssl True Verify TLS certificates for admin/HTTP calls default_timeout 60 Request timeout in seconds extra_headers None Extra HTTP headers for admin/HTTP calls

The underlying python-arango handles are available as graph.client and graph.db.

docs.title: A. Databases
docs.text:
Database operations always run against _system, using the same credentials as the client.

graph.list_databases()                 # ['_system', 'knowledge', ...]
graph.create_database("knowledge")     # True
graph.delete_database("old_db")        # True

graph.switch_db("knowledge")           # reuses the stored credentials

docs.title: B. Collections (documents and edges)
docs.text:
Vertices are stored in document collections; edges are stored in edge collections (edge=True).

graph.create_collection("people")
graph.create_collection("knows", edge=True)

# Create only if missing
graph.ensure_collection("companies")
graph.ensure_collection("works_at", edge=True)

graph.has_collection("people")         # True
col = graph.get_collection("people")   # python-arango Collection
graph.delete_collection("old")         # ignore_missing=True by default

create_collection also accepts cluster and schema options: replication_factor, write_concern, number_of_shards, shard_keys, key_options, schema, plus any extra python-arango keyword arguments.

docs.title: C. Documents and edges (CRUD)
docs.text:
graph.insert_one("people", {"_key": "alice", "name": "Alice"})
graph.insert_one("people", {"_key": "bob", "name": "Bob"})

# Edge: _from / _to reference vertex IDs ("<collection>/<key>")
graph.insert_one("knows", {"_from": "people/alice", "_to": "people/bob", "since": 2020})

graph.get_one("people", "alice")       # {'_key': 'alice', 'name': 'Alice'}  (_id/_rev stripped), or None
graph.update_one("people", {"_key": "alice", "age": 31})          # merge update
graph.replace_one("people", {"_key": "alice", "name": "Alice B."})
graph.delete_one("people", "bob")      # True / False

Batched writes:

graph.insert_many("people", docs, overwrite=False, batch_size=1000)
# -> {"inserted": <n>, "errors": <n>}

graph.upsert_many("people", docs, on="_key", update_expr="MERGE(OLD, NEW)", batch_size=1000)
# -> number of documents processed; every doc must contain the `on` field

docs.title: D. Querying with AQL
docs.text:
friends = graph.aql(
    """
    FOR v, e IN 1..2 OUTBOUND @start knows
      RETURN { name: v.name, since: e.since }
    """,
    bind_vars={"start": "people/alice"},
)

aql() returns the full result as a list.

docs.title: E. Bulk ingestion
docs.text:
From Python iterables (bulk import API):

graph.http_bulk_import(
    collection="people",
    docs=docs,
    on_duplicate="update",     # "error" | "update" | "replace" | "ignore"
    batch_size=5000,
)
# -> {"created": n, "updated": n, "ignored": n, "errors": n}

graph.http_bulk_import(collection="people", jsonl_path="/data/people.jsonl")

From a local file (JSON array or JSONL):

graph.ingest_from_file("people", "/data/people.jsonl")                            # insert_many
graph.ingest_from_file("people", "/data/people.json", upsert_on="_key")           # upsert
graph.ingest_from_file("people", "/data/people.jsonl", use_http_bulk=True,
                       on_duplicate="replace")                                    # bulk import
graph.ingest_from_file("people", "/data/raw.jsonl",
                       transform=lambda d: {"_key": d["id"], "name": d["full_name"]})

From S3 (JSON array or JSONL object):

graph.ingest_from_s3(
    "people",
    bucket="my-bucket",
    key="exports/people.jsonl",
    aws_region="us-east-1",          # else AWS_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION
    upsert_on="_key",
)

Credentials default to the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables. All ingest methods return a stats dict with a method key (insert_many, upsert or http_bulk_import).

docs.title: F. Admin helpers
docs.text:
graph.server_status()     # GET  /_admin/status
graph.server_role()       # GET  /_admin/server/role
graph.cluster_health()    # GET  /_admin/cluster/health
graph.routing_reload()    # POST /_admin/routing/reload

graph.run_admin_command("/_api/version", method="GET")

docs.title: Example: Knowledge Graph in an Agent
docs.text:
from agent_addons.graph import ArangoSDK

graph = ArangoSDK(endpoint="http://localhost:8529", db_name="knowledge",
                  username="root", password="secret")

graph.ensure_collection("entities")
graph.ensure_collection("relations", edge=True)

graph.upsert_many("entities", [
    {"_key": "acme", "type": "company", "name": "Acme Corp"},
    {"_key": "retailco", "type": "company", "name": "RetailCo"},
])
graph.insert_one("relations", {"_from": "entities/acme", "_to": "entities/retailco",
                               "type": "supplies"})

partners = graph.aql(
    "FOR v IN 1..1 ANY @start relations RETURN v.name",
    bind_vars={"start": "entities/acme"},
)
print(partners)   # ['RetailCo']

docs.title: Agent LLM Interface — Client Developer Documentation
Introduction
docs.text:
Agents call LLMs and other AI models through two libraries:

Library Package Use it for LLM Interface agents_llm (libs/llm-interface) Full inference client. Calls AIOS blocks over gRPC or REST, AIOS vDAGs, OpenAI, or custom backends. Supports infer, chat completions, completions, multipart inference, async calls, block pre/post-processing policies, latency metrics and LLM-based selection LLM Interface Lite agents_llm_lite (libs/llm-interface-lite) A simple prompt-in / text-out registry of inference providers (AIOS or OpenAI). Includes generate-and-execute for code

A typical workflow is:

  1. Declare a ModelItem in the Subject Specification (optional) to record which models the agent uses.
  2. Create a client and register one or more backends under names.
  3. Run inference by backend name.

docs.title: Registering LLMs in Subject Specification
docs.text: Models can be recorded in the subject's integrations.models list using ModelItem.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Any

@dataclass
class ModelItem:
    llm_type: str
    llm_block_id: str
    llm_selection_query: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    llm_parameters: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "llm_type": "inference",
  "llm_block_id": "gemma3-27b-block",
  "llm_selection_query": {},
  "llm_parameters": {
    "network_host": "34.93.251.223",
    "inference_server_id": "inference-server-1",
    "mode": "auto"
  }
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text:
Field Type Description llm_type str Model kind, e.g. "inference". llm_block_id str AIOS block ID (model) or provider model name. llm_selection_query dict Optional selector for picking a deployment. llm_parameters dict Backend settings, e.g. network_host, inference_server_id, mode.

The agents SDK does not build LLM clients from ModelItem entries automatically. Read them from self.subject.integrations.models and register backends yourself (see below).

docs.title: Import and Setup
docs.text:
from agents_llm import AIGridClient
from agents_llm.custom import AbstractBlockInferenceSystem, OpenAIBlockInferenceSystem

client = AIGridClient()

AIGridClient keeps a registry of inference systems by name. Methods called without name= use the system registered as "default".

docs.title: A. AIOS block (gRPC or REST)
docs.text:
client.add_block(
    name="gemma",
    network_host="34.93.251.223",            # host of the AIOS registries
    inference_server_id="inference-server-1",
    model="gemma3-27b-block",                # block ID
    mode="auto",                             # "auto" | "grpc" | "rest"
)

How the block is resolved:

  1. Inference server. If inference_server_id is set, the server record is fetched from the inference server registry at http://<network_host>:30105. Its inference_server_urls give the REST URL (rest / http / https, else inference_server_public_url) and the gRPC address (grpc / grpc_address / grpc_url).
  2. Direct URLs. If inference_server_id="", pass urls={"rest": "http://...:31504"} and/or urls={"grpc": "host:port"} instead.
  3. Transport. mode="auto" picks gRPC when available, else REST. Asking for a transport that isn't available raises RuntimeError.
  4. Block data. The block record is fetched from the blocks registry at http://<network_host>:30100. If it defines policies named agents_pre_processing / agents_post_processing, they run on every request payload and response.
# Direct REST URL, no inference server registry lookup
client.add_block(
    name="gemma-rest",
    network_host="34.93.251.223",
    inference_server_id="",
    model="gemma3-27b-block",
    mode="rest",
    urls={"rest": "http://35.232.150.117:31504"},
)

default_headers (optional) are sent to the inference server registry.

docs.title: B. AIOS vDAG
docs.text:
client.add_vdag(
    name="pipeline",
    registry_base_url="http://<vdag-controller-registry>",
    vdag_uri="my-vdag:1.0-stable",
    mode="auto",
)

All vDAG controllers registered for vdag_uri are listed and one is picked at random. Its REST and gRPC endpoints come from config.urls (rest/http/https, else public_url; grpc, else config.grpc_address/config.grpc_url).

docs.title: C. OpenAI
docs.text:
openai_llm = OpenAIBlockInferenceSystem(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",          # default
    api_key=None,                 # default: OPENAI_API_KEY (required)
    base_url=None,                # optional OpenAI-compatible endpoint
    organization=None,
    project=None,
)
client.add_custom_block(name="openai", system=openai_llm)
  • Only OpenAI-supported keys are forwarded from data. Chat: messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, n, stop, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, logit_bias, user, tools, tool_choice, response_format, seed, metadata. Text: the same, minus tools/tool_choice/response_format, plus prompt.
  • infer() routes to chat when data contains messages (or is a list of role/content dicts), and to text completions when it contains prompt (or is a string or list). If the model does not support text completions, the call is retried as a chat completion.
  • Multipart inference is not supported.

docs.title: D. Custom backends
docs.text: See Writing a Custom Backend.

docs.title: Managing backends
docs.text:
client.list()            # ['gemma', 'openai', ...]
system = client.get("gemma")
client.remove("gemma")

docs.title: Chat completions
docs.text:
resp = client.chat_completions(
    name="openai",
    session_id="sess-001",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in one paragraph."}],
    data={"temperature": 0.2, "max_tokens": 256},
)
print(resp["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])

For AIOS blocks, messages is merged into data (data["messages"] = messages). The pre-processing policy (if any) runs on data, and the result is sent to POST /v1/chat/completions (REST) or the gRPC chat_completions call. Generation settings for the block go in data, for example:

resp = client.chat_completions(
    name="gemma-rest",
    session_id="session-1214",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2 + 2?"}],
    data={
        "mode": "chat",
        "generation_config": {"max_new_tokens": 512, "do_sample": False, "top_p": 0.95, "temperature": 1.0},
    },
)

docs.title: Completions
docs.text:
resp = client.completions(name="gemma", session_id="sess-002",
                          prompts="Write a haiku about the ocean", data={})

For AIOS blocks, always pass a dict as data (the prompt is added to it as data["prompt"]).

client.completions(...) currently fails with a TypeError for OpenAI and other custom systems: AIGridClient always passes data=, which AbstractBlockInferenceSystem.completions does not accept. Call the system directly instead — client.get("openai").completions(prompt="...", session_id="sess-002") — or use chat completions.

docs.title: Raw inference
docs.text:
resp = client.infer(name="gemma", session_id="sess-003", data={"mode": "chat", "message": "Hello"})

For AIOS blocks this calls POST /v1/infer (or gRPC infer) with model, session_id, seq_no, data, files, graph and selection_query.

docs.title: Multipart inference (files)
docs.text:
resp = client.infer_multipart(name="gemma-rest", session_id="sess-004", data={"mode": "vision"})

Multipart is only available over REST (POST /v1/infer-multipart).

docs.title: Full-parameter calls
docs.text:
The simplified methods above always send seq_no=0 and no files, graph, selection_query, frame_ptr or output_ptr. To set these, use the internal_* methods. They pass keyword arguments straight to the backend:

client.internal_infer(
    name="gemma",
    session_id="sess-005",
    seq_no=7,
    data={"mode": "chat", "message": "Describe this image"},
    files=["/tmp/cat.png"],
    selection_query={},
    graph={},
)

vDAG systems take a smaller set of arguments (for example, infer(session_id, seq_no, data, files, frame_ptr, ts)), so call them through internal_* methods or client.get(name) rather than the simplified methods.

docs.title: Async calls
docs.text:
Every call has an async variant (async_infer, async_chat_completions, async_completions, async_infer_multipart, plus internal_async_*). Each runs in a background thread and returns a ResultWaiter:

waiter = client.async_chat_completions(
    name="openai",
    session_id="sess-006",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2 + 2?"}],
    data={},
)
waiter.ready()                 # True once finished
resp = waiter.wait(timeout=30) # raises TimeoutError, or re-raises the call's exception

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Each system keeps rolling latency metrics:

client.get("gemma").get_metrics()
# {"count": 12, "last_latency": 0.41, "min_latency": 0.32, "max_latency": 1.2, "avg_latency": 0.47}

docs.title: LLM-based Selection (SelectionEngine)
docs.text:
SelectionEngine asks a model to pick the single best candidate for a query. Candidates are any objects with an id and a get_searchable_representation() method.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List

@dataclass
class Shoe:
    id: str
    title: str
    tags: List[str]

    def get_searchable_representation(self) -> str:
        return f"title={self.title}; tags={','.join(self.tags)}"

engine = client.create_selector(name="openai", base_query="Select the best product for the user.")

result = engine.select(
    entities=[Shoe("A1", "Red Running Shoes", ["running"]), Shoe("B2", "Trail Shoes", ["trail"])],
    user_query="I need running shoes for daily jogging.",
    session_id="sess-007",
    extra_data={"max_tokens": 64},
)
result.selected_id   # "A1"
result.raw_json      # {"id": "A1"}

The engine sends a chat completion with strict JSON-only instructions and response_format={"type": "json_object"}, temperature=0.0, max_tokens=32 (overridable through extra_data). It parses {"id": ...} from the reply. ValueError is raised if the reply isn't valid JSON or the ID is not one of the candidates.

docs.title: Writing a Custom Backend
docs.text:
Subclass AbstractBlockInferenceSystem and implement the four _do_* hooks. The base class provides the public infer / chat_completions / completions / infer_multipart methods, their async variants, and latency metrics.

from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
from agents_llm.custom import AbstractBlockInferenceSystem


class EchoLLM(AbstractBlockInferenceSystem):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(model="echo")

    def _do_infer(self, *, session_id, seq_no, data, files, selection_query, graph, frame_ptr, output_ptr):
        return {"reply": data}

    def _do_chat_completions(self, *, messages, session_id, seq_no, selection_query, graph,
                             frame_ptr, output_ptr, data=None):
        last = messages[-1]["content"] if messages else ""
        return {"choices": [{"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": last}}]}

    def _do_completions(self, *, prompt, session_id, seq_no, selection_query, graph,
                        frame_ptr, output_ptr, data=None):
        return {"choices": [{"text": prompt}]}

    def _do_infer_multipart(self, *, session_id, seq_no, data, ts, frame_ptr, files):
        raise RuntimeError("not supported")


client.add_custom_block(name="echo", system=EchoLLM())

Optional hooks:

  • _finalize_mode() — resolve mode ("auto" → "grpc"/"rest") at construction.
  • _check_mode(operation) — reject operations the transport doesn't support.

docs.title: Block Discovery
docs.text:
BlockSearchClient queries the AIOS search service for blocks:

from agents_llm.discovery import BlockSearchClient

search = BlockSearchClient("http://<search-service>")
search.filter_query(filter={"tags": "llm"})                          # POST /api/filter
search.search(policyRuleURI="policies/rank-blocks:1.0-stable",       # POST /api/search
              filter={"tags": "llm"}, policy_params={})

docs.title: Part 2 — agents_llm_lite (LLM Interface Lite)
docs.text:
agents_llm_lite is a registry of simple text-generation providers. Every provider implements:

infer(*, prompt, callback, temperature=0.1, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=4096, system_message=None, **kwargs) -> str

callback(raw_response) -> str extracts the text from the provider's raw response. Markdown fences are stripped from the result.

from agents_llm_lite.inference import AgentInferenceManager
from agents_llm_lite.custom import BaseInference, OpenAIInference

llm = AgentInferenceManager()

docs.title: AIOS provider
docs.text:
llm.register_new_inference(
    name="aios",
    model="magistral-small-2506-llama-cpp-block",
    inference_server_id="http://35.232.150.117:31504",   # or a registry ID
    aios_url_map={"inference_server_url": "http://<registry>", "blocks_db_url": "http://<blocks-db>"},
    system_message="You are a concise assistant.",
)

text = llm.infer(
    name="aios",
    prompt="Summarize the benefits of vector databases.",
    callback=lambda raw: raw["data"]["reply"],
)

The request is POST /v1/infer with data = {"mode": "chat", "gen_params": {temperature, top_p, max_tokens}, "message": prompt, "system_message": ...}.

docs.title: OpenAI provider
docs.text:
llm.register_custom_inference(name="openai", provider=OpenAIInference(model="gpt-4o-mini"))

text = llm.infer(
    name="openai",
    prompt="Write a haiku about the ocean",
    callback=lambda resp: resp.choices[0].message.content,
)

OpenAIInference uses OPENAI_API_KEY unless you pass client=OpenAI(...). It sends max_tokens as max_completion_tokens, and does not forward temperature or top_p.

docs.title: Generate and execute
docs.text:
infer_and_execute works like the Code Generator SDK's generate_and_execute: it generates code, installs declared requirements, loads the code as a module, and calls main (or class_name().method_name, or a single callable class):

result = llm.infer_and_execute(
    name="aios",
    prompt="Write `def main(a, b)` returning the element-wise sum of two lists.",
    callback=lambda raw: raw["data"]["reply"],
    args=[[1, 2], [3, 4]],
)

docs.title: Managing providers
docs.text:
llm.list_inferences()
llm.has_inference("openai")
llm.get_inference("openai")
llm.unregister_inference("openai")
llm.clear_inferences()

Custom providers subclass BaseInference (keyword-only model, session_id, logger, default_system_message) and implement infer. Lite providers can also be used as the llm of AgentRAG (see Accessing Vector Databases).

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep API keys in environment variables (OPENAI_API_KEY) rather than in code or subject specs.
  • Use async_* calls with ResultWaiter.wait(timeout=...) to bound waiting time.
  • Use block pre/post-processing policies to adapt payloads per model without changing agent code.
  • Use get_metrics() to monitor backend latency.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Agent memories let agents store, retrieve, and share context, knowledge, and events. There are three practical classes of memory:

  1. SDK Context Store — namespaced key-value memory built into the agents SDK (core.context), backed by local Redis, a global Redis, a shared Redis or an in-process store. It includes helpers for sessions, conversation history, working memory, tool state, checkpoints and more.
  2. Agent Context Cache — in-process key-value working state whose updates are broadcast to NATS topics (agent_context_cache, in libs/agents-addons).
  3. Memory Grid — FrameDB-based in-memory, storage and streaming backends (see the Memory Grid section).

For long-term episodic, semantic, procedural, reflective and reward memory, git-versioned agent files, and learning lessons from experience (mining, human review, applying lessons, feedback), see Advanced Agent Memories.

Memory Type Purpose / Use Case Best for SDK Context Store (core.context.store.RedisStore) Namespaced get/set with TTLs and automatic serialization. Local, global or shared scope. Session-structured helpers (AgentSession, ConversationMemory, WorkingMemory, CheckpointManager, …). The agent's primary working memory: conversation history, active plan and steps, tool state, checkpoints. Use the global or shared store to share state between instances and agents. Agent Context Cache (AgentContextCache) Namespace-scoped in-process get/set. Every write is queued and broadcast over NATS to configured topics. Small, fast-changing state that other agents must be notified about (coordination flags, shared context updates). Data is not persisted. Memory Grid (memory_type="memory-grid") FrameDB-backed in-memory objects, durable storage and streams. Large objects, durable results and event streams.

docs.title: Registering Memory in Subject Specification
docs.text: Memories can be recorded in the subject's integrations.memory_systems list using MemoryItem. The agents SDK does not instantiate memories from these entries automatically. Read them from self.subject.integrations.memory_systems and create the store in your agent.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
@dataclass
class MemoryItem:
    memory_id: str
    memory_type: str = ""
    memory_backend: str = ""
    memory_custom_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "memory_id": "context-memory-01",
  "memory_type": "agent-context",
  "memory_backend": "redis-shared",
  "memory_custom_config": {
    "redis_url": "redis://redis.default.svc.cluster.local:6379/0",
    "namespace": "agent-alpha"
  }
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text: Field Type Description memory_id str Unique identifier for this memory entry. memory_type str Type of memory (e.g. "agent-context", "memory-grid"). memory_backend str Backend the agent should create (your own convention, e.g. "redis-local", "redis-global", "redis-shared", "in-memory"). memory_custom_config dict Backend settings (e.g. redis_url, namespace).

docs.title: SDK Context Store — Client Developer Documentation
Introduction
docs.text: The agents SDK includes a key-value store at core.context.store.RedisStore, plus higher-level memory helpers in core.context.utils, core.context.io and core.context.workspace. Every helper is built on RedisStore namespaces, so the same code works against an in-process store or Redis.

docs.title: Stores
docs.text:
from core.context.store import RedisStore

local = RedisStore.get_local_store()                  # redis://localhost:6379 (the instance's Redis sidecar)
mem = RedisStore.get_local_store(in_memory=True)      # in-process store, no Redis needed (only if no local store exists yet)
glob = RedisStore.get_global_store()                  # Redis at REDIS_GLOBAL_STORE_HOST_URL
shared = RedisStore.get_shared_store("redis://redis.shared:6379/0")
Store Backend Scope Local (get_local_store()) redis://localhost:6379, or an in-process dict when in_memory=True One agent instance Global (get_global_store()) Redis at REDIS_GLOBAL_STORE_HOST_URL (RuntimeError if unset) All agents configured with that URL Shared (get_shared_store(url)) Redis at url Anyone with the URL

Each store is a process-wide singleton: one local store, one global store, and one shared store per URL. The first call to get_local_store decides whether the local store is in-memory or Redis.

docs.title: Basic Operations
docs.text:
store = RedisStore.get_local_store().get_namespace("agent-alpha")

store.set("plan", ["fetch", "summarize"])
store.set("token", "abc", ex=3600)        # expires in 1 hour
store.get("plan")                         # ['fetch', 'summarize']
store.get("missing", default={})          # {}
store.exists("plan")                      # True
store.pop("token")                        # get and delete
store.update({"a": 1, "b": 2.5})          # bulk set
store.keys()                              # keys in this namespace (and its sub-namespaces)
store.items(); store.values()
store.delete("a")
store.clear()                             # delete all keys under this namespace

store["mode"] = "auto"; "mode" in store; len(store); del store["mode"]
  • get_namespace(name) returns a child store whose keys are prefixed parent:name:. Namespaces nest.
  • Values keep their type: None, bytes, str, bool, int and float are stored natively; dict/list/tuple as JSON (tuples come back as lists); anything else is pickled.

docs.title: Memory Helpers
docs.text:
All helpers take a store (or a session) and keep their data in namespaces under it.

from core.context.utils import (
    AgentSession, ConversationMemory, WorkingMemory, ToolState, ExecutionLock,
    InterruptState, WorkflowState, MetricsState, CheckpointManager, PromptContextBuilder,
)

session = AgentSession(RedisStore.get_global_store(), agent_id="agent-alpha", session_id="sess-1")

AgentSession stores everything under agents:<agent_id>:sessions:<session_id>, with sub-namespaces meta, messages, working, tools, metrics, workflow, interrupts, checkpoints and locks. It records created and status (active) on first use, and provides status(), set_status(), touch(), reset(), export() and import_state().

Helper Main methods Use for ConversationMemory(session) add(role, content), get_all(), get_recent(n), update(i, content), delete(i), summarize(text), get_summary(), clear() Conversation history and a running summary WorkingMemory(session) set/get/delete, set_goal/get_goal, set_plan/get_plan, set_step, complete_step, state() Goal, plan and step tracking ToolState(session) set_pending, resolve, set_history, history(), pending(), last_result() Pending tool calls and tool history ExecutionLock(session) acquire(owner, ttl=60), release(owner), owner(), is_locked(), force_release() Ensuring one worker processes a session at a time InterruptState(session) wait_for(event), resolve(data), waiting(), result() Waiting for human or external input WorkflowState(session) set_current, complete_node, completed(), is_complete(), mark_complete() Tracking workflow progress MetricsState(session) inc, record_latency, record_tokens, avg_latency(), stats() Per-session counters CheckpointManager(session) snapshot() → id, restore(id), list(), delete(id) Saving and restoring messages, working memory, tools, workflow and metrics PromptContextBuilder(session) build(max_messages=20), build_flat_text() Building LLM prompt context from session memory 
convo = ConversationMemory(session)
convo.add("user", "Summarize the contract.")
convo.add("assistant", "Here is the summary...")

work = WorkingMemory(session)
work.set_goal("Review contract")
work.set_plan(["extract", "analyze", "report"])

cid = CheckpointManager(session).snapshot()

prompt_ctx = PromptContextBuilder(session).build(max_messages=10)

Other helpers built on a store:

Helper Module Description IOChannel(store, name) core.context.io Request/response channel: submit(input) → id, fetch_input(), set_output(id, output), wait_for_output(id, timeout=60), get_status(id), cleanup(id) TaskQueue(store, name="default") core.context.workspace Simple queue: enqueue(task) → id, dequeue(), retry(id) SharedWorkspace(store, name="global") core.context.workspace publish(key, value) (keeps an event history), subscribe(key) StreamingBuffer(store, name) core.context.workspace Token streaming: start(), append(token), complete(), get_partial()

These helpers do read-modify-write on whole values (for example, the message list), so concurrent writers to the same session can overwrite each other. Use ExecutionLock when several workers may touch one session.

docs.title: Agent Context Cache Memory
docs.text:
The Agent Context Cache (agent_context_cache, in libs/agents-addons) keeps namespaced key-value data in process memory and broadcasts every write to NATS topics.

from agent_context_cache.core.agent_context import AgentContextCache

ctx = AgentContextCache()

ctx.set("user_profile", {"name": "Alice", "age": 30})
ctx.get("user_profile")                              # {'name': 'Alice', 'age': 30}

ctx.set("session_token", "abc123", namespace="auth")
ctx.list_keys(namespace="auth")
ctx.list_namespaces()
ctx.clear_namespace("auth")

ctx.set_topics_list(["agent.context.updates"])       # broadcast topics (NATS at nats://localhost:4222)

Each write is published to every configured topic as:

{
  "event_type": "context_update",
  "sender_subject_id": "<SUBJECT_ID>",
  "event_data": { "operation": "set", "namespace": "default", "key": "user_profile", "value": { "name": "Alice", "age": 30 } }
}

Data is not persisted. enable_backup() and set_backup_settings() only store configuration; no backup is performed. The package currently has import and shutdown issues. See Agent Context Cache for the full reference and known issues.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The Memory Grid is the integration layer between an agent and distributed FrameDB instances. It allows the agent to maintain and access different kinds of memory through a single, consistent API.

Memory Grid supports three backend modes:

  • in-memory — Fast, volatile storage for ephemeral data.
  • storage — Persistent object storage for long-term retention.
  • streaming — Ordered queues for real-time event processing.

All modes use the same FrameDBClient interface for storing, retrieving, streaming, and backing up data.

A typical workflow is:

  1. Declare a Memory Grid entry in the agent’s subject specification.
  2. Initialize the FrameDB client with cluster and routing URLs.
  3. Perform operations according to the backend type.
  4. Optionally back up or restore memory between instances or external storage.

docs.title: Registering Memory Grid in Subject Specification
docs.text: A Memory Grid is declared in the subject specification using the MemoryItem structure. The memory_type must be "memory-grid", and the memory_backend specifies which mode to use.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Any

@dataclass
class MemoryItem:
    memory_id: str
    memory_type: str = "memory-grid"   # Fixed value
    memory_backend: str = ""           # "in-memory", "storage", or "streaming"
    memory_custom_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Minimal Required Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "memory_id": "memory-grid-01",
  "memory_type": "memory-grid",
  "memory_backend": "in-memory",
  "memory_custom_config": {
    "framedb_id": "framedb-inmem-1",
    "cluster_url": "http://framedb-cluster",
    "routing_url": "http://routing-service"
  }
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text: Field Location Type Description memory_id root str Unique identifier for this memory entry in the subject spec. memory_type root str Must be "memory-grid" for Memory Grid integration. memory_backend root str Memory mode — "in-memory", "storage", or "streaming". memory_custom_config.framedb_id config str Target FrameDB instance ID. memory_custom_config.cluster_url config str Base API URL for the FrameDB cluster. memory_custom_config.routing_url config str API URL for the FrameDB routing service. memory_custom_config.extra_params config dict Optional backend-specific settings (e.g., cache size, credentials).

docs.title: Import and Setup
docs.text:
from framedb_sdk import FrameDBClient

client = FrameDBClient(
    cluster_url="http://framedb-cluster",
    routing_url="http://routing-service"
)

docs.title: In-Memory Backend (memory_backend="in-memory")
docs.text:
Purpose: Fast, volatile memory backed by Redis for temporary state, shared context, or scratchpad data.

Example:

client.set_object({
    "key": "session:123",
    "data": b"ephemeral binary data",
    "framedb_id": "framedb-inmem-1",
    "type": "in-memory"
})

result = client.get_object("session:123")
print(result["object"]["data"])

Notes:

  • Data is not persisted after restart.
  • Use create_backup(...) to persist important data.

docs.title: Storage Backend (memory_backend="storage")
docs.text:
Purpose: Persistent object storage backed by TiDB or another SQL-compatible DB.

Example:

client.set_pythonic_object(
    key="model_snapshot_v1",
    obj={"weights": [1, 2, 3]},
    framedb_id="framedb-storage-1",
    framedb_type="storage"
)

res = client.get_pythonic_object("model_snapshot_v1")
print(res["object"]["python_object"])

Notes:

  • Supports long-term retention and backups to object stores.

docs.title: Streaming Backend (memory_backend="streaming")
docs.text:
Purpose: Ordered queues backed by Redis Streams for event-driven workflows.

Example — Continuous Listener:

for msg in client.listen_for_stream_data("agent-events", "framedb-stream-1"):
    print("New event:", msg)

Example — Bulk Pull:

for msg in client.pull_all_stream_data("agent-events", "framedb-stream-1"):
    print("Event:", msg)

Notes:

  • Maintains strict ordering.
  • Suitable for live ingestion or inter-agent communication.

docs.title: Backup & Restore
docs.text:
# Backup a single key
client.create_backup("session:123", "framedb-backup-1")

# Restore from backup
client.restore_from_backup(
    keys=["session:123"],
    framedb_id="framedb-inmem-1",
    framedb_type="in-memory",
    s3_credentials_dict={
        "bucket": "my-bucket",
        "access_key": "...",
        "secret_key": "...",
        "region": "ap-south-1"
    }
)

docs.title: Agent Application Metrics
docs.text: This document describes the AgentsMetrics class from the agent_core_libs package. It collects a standard set of agent runtime metrics, exposes them in Prometheus format over HTTP, and periodically pushes JSON snapshots to Redis.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
AgentsMetrics provides:

  • Four standard Prometheus metrics: latency, queue length, tasks processed and throughput (FPS).
  • Rolling summaries (current value and 1m / 5m / 15m averages) for latency, FPS and any custom series you record.
  • Push-based snapshots to a Redis list for centralized collection.
  • Hardware metrics (CPU, memory, load average) in each snapshot, when psutil is installed.
  • Automatic labels: agentID, instanceID and nodeID.
  • A built-in HTTP exporter for Prometheus scraping.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
AgentsMetrics is part of agent_core_libs (libs/core-libs), which depends on redis and prometheus-client. Install the optional metrics-hw extra to include hardware metrics:

pip install "./libs/core-libs[metrics-hw]"

docs.title: Importing
docs.text: from agent_core_libs.metrics import AgentsMetrics

docs.title: Standard Metrics
docs.text:
Prometheus name Type Updated by Description agent_latency_seconds Histogram observe_latency(seconds) End-to-end latency in seconds agent_queue_length Gauge set_queue_length(n) Current queue length agent_tasks_processed_total Counter inc_tasks_processed(n=1) Total number of tasks processed agent_fps Gauge set_fps(fps) Throughput (frames/s or items/s)

The default histogram buckets are (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10).

Each metric carries these labels:

Label Source agentID agent_id argument, else AGENT_ID env (default test-agent) instanceID instance_id argument, else INSTANCE_ID env (default agent-instance-001) nodeID NODE_ID env, else HOSTNAME env, else node-unknown

docs.title: 1. Initialize
docs.text:
metrics = AgentsMetrics(agent_id="subject-xyz", prometheus_port=8889)

All arguments are keyword-only and optional:

Argument Default / env fallback Description agent_id AGENT_ID (test-agent) Agent identifier label instance_id INSTANCE_ID (agent-instance-001) Instance identifier label redis_host METRICS_REDIS_HOST (localhost) Redis host for snapshots redis_port METRICS_REDIS_PORT (6379) Redis port redis_db METRICS_REDIS_DB (0) Redis DB redis_list_key AGENT_METRICS_LIST (AGENT_METRICS) Redis list that receives snapshots push_interval_sec 30 (the AGENT_METRICS_PUSH_INTERVAL env overrides it) Seconds between snapshots prometheus_port None If set, start the HTTP exporter immediately histogram_buckets see above Latency histogram buckets

The Redis snapshot writer starts as soon as the object is created. The metrics are registered in the global Prometheus registry, so create only one AgentsMetrics per process.

docs.title: 2. Update the standard metrics
docs.text:
metrics.observe_latency(0.42)
metrics.set_queue_length(7)
metrics.inc_tasks_processed()      # +1
metrics.inc_tasks_processed(5)     # +5
metrics.set_fps(24.5)

observe_latency and set_fps also feed the rolling series latency_seconds and fps.

docs.title: 3. Record custom rolling metrics
docs.text:
Custom series are grouped by category. They are included in snapshots, but are not exported to Prometheus.

metrics.observe_custom_rolling("llm", "tokens_per_second", 85.2)
metrics.observe_custom_rolling("llm", "prompt_tokens", 512)

docs.title: 4. Read rolling summaries
docs.text:
metrics.get_extended_metrics()

{
  "latency_seconds": { "current": 0.42, "average_1m": 0.40, "average_5m": 0.38, "average_15m": 0.37 },
  "fps":             { "current": 24.5, "average_1m": 24.1, "average_5m": 23.9, "average_15m": 24.0 },
  "custom": {
    "llm": {
      "tokens_per_second": { "current": 85.2, "average_1m": 85.2, "average_5m": 85.2, "average_15m": 85.2 }
    }
  }
}

Rolling series keep 15 minutes of samples.

docs.title: Prometheus exporter
docs.text:
metrics.start_http_server(port=8889)

This starts a Prometheus HTTP endpoint at http://<host>:<port>/metrics on a background thread. If METRICS_PORT is set in the environment, it overrides the port argument. Passing prometheus_port to the constructor does the same thing.

docs.title: Redis snapshots
docs.text:
Every push_interval_sec seconds, a JSON snapshot is LPUSHed to the Redis list (AGENT_METRICS by default):

{
  "agentId": "subject-xyz",
  "instanceId": "agent-instance-001",
  "nodeId": "agent-node-123",
  "type": "agent",
  "timestamp": 1735689600.12,

  "agent_latency_seconds_bucket": 2.0,
  "agent_latency_seconds_count": 12.0,
  "agent_latency_seconds_sum": 4.9,
  "agent_queue_length": 7.0,
  "agent_tasks_processed_total": 6.0,
  "agent_fps": 24.5,

  "hardware": {
    "cpu_percent": 12.5,
    "mem_total": 16777216000,
    "mem_used": 8388608000,
    "mem_free": 8388608000,
    "mem_percent": 50.0,
    "load_avg": [0.5, 0.4, 0.3]
  },

  "latency_seconds": { "current": 0.42, "average_1m": 0.40, "average_5m": 0.38, "average_15m": 0.37 },
  "fps": { "current": 24.5, "average_1m": 24.1, "average_5m": 23.9, "average_15m": 24.0 },
  "custom": { "llm": { "...": "..." } }
}
  • Prometheus samples are flattened by sample name (_created samples are skipped). Because sample names are the keys, only one value is kept per name; for the histogram, that is the last bucket.
  • hardware is {} if psutil is not installed.
  • Redis errors while pushing are ignored.

docs.title: Stop
docs.text: metrics.stop()   # stops the Redis writer (waits up to 5 s)

docs.title: Agent Object Storage
docs.text: This document describes how to use the S3Storage class from the agent_core_libs package to work with an S3-compatible object storage backend (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph, etc.).

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
S3Storage is a thin wrapper around boto3 that provides:

  • Uploads from a file path, bytes, a file object, or a JSON-serializable object.
  • Downloads to a file path, a file object, bytes, or parsed JSON.
  • Server-side copy and move.
  • Deleting single objects or everything under a prefix.
  • Listing and iterating objects, reading metadata, and existence checks.
  • Bucket helpers and presigned URLs.

It supports:

  • Access-key and session-token authentication.
  • Custom endpoints (MinIO and other S3-compatible stores), with optional path-style addressing.
  • Automatic retries (standard retry mode) and multipart transfers for large files.

All methods log success, and log then re-raise botocore ClientError / BotoCoreError on failure.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
S3Storage is part of agent_core_libs (libs/core-libs), which depends on boto3>=1.34.0.

pip install ./libs/core-libs

docs.title: Import
docs.text: from agent_core_libs.storage import S3Storage

docs.title: Initialize the client
docs.text:
All arguments are keyword-only.

store = S3Storage(
    access_key_id="your-access-key",
    secret_access_key="your-secret-key",
    region_name="us-east-1",
)
Argument Default Description access_key_id — (required) Access key secret_access_key — (required) Secret key region_name "us-east-1" Region session_token None Session token for temporary credentials endpoint_url None Custom S3 endpoint (e.g. MinIO) max_attempts 10 Maximum retry attempts multipart_threshold_mb 8 Use multipart transfers above this size (MB) multipart_chunksize_mb 8 Multipart chunk size (MB) use_path_style False Use path-style addressing (endpoint/bucket/key) logger module logger Custom logging.Logger

docs.title: Upload a file from a path
docs.text:
store.upload_file("my-bucket", "my-folder/my-file.txt", "/path/to/local/file.txt")

# With extra S3 arguments
store.upload_file(
    "my-bucket", "docs/report.pdf", "/tmp/report.pdf",
    extra_args={"ContentType": "application/pdf", "ACL": "private"},
)

docs.title: Upload bytes
docs.text: store.upload_bytes("my-bucket", "data/hello.txt", b"Hello, world!")

docs.title: Upload from a file object (e.g. BytesIO)
docs.text:
import io

buffer = io.BytesIO(b"Buffered content")
store.upload_fileobj("my-bucket", "buffer/file.txt", buffer)

docs.title: Upload JSON
docs.text:
store.put_json("my-bucket", "configs/settings.json", {"threshold": 0.8})
# Stored with ContentType "application/json"

docs.title: Download to a local path
docs.text: store.download_file("my-bucket", "my-folder/my-file.txt", "/path/to/save/file.txt")

docs.title: Download to a file object
docs.text:
import io

output_buffer = io.BytesIO()
store.download_to_fileobj("my-bucket", "data/hello.txt", output_buffer)
print(output_buffer.getvalue())

docs.title: Download as bytes
docs.text:
data = store.download_as_bytes("my-bucket", "data/hello.txt")
print(data.decode())

docs.title: Read JSON
docs.text: settings = store.get_json("my-bucket", "configs/settings.json")

docs.title: Copy and move
docs.text:
store.copy_object("src-bucket", "a/file.txt", "dest-bucket", "b/file.txt")
store.move_object("src-bucket", "a/file.txt", "dest-bucket", "b/file.txt")  # copy, then delete source

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
store.delete_object("my-bucket", "data/hello.txt")

deleted_count = store.delete_prefix("my-bucket", "tmp/")   # deletes in batches of 1000

docs.title: List and inspect objects
docs.text:
objects = store.list_objects("my-bucket", prefix="data/", max_keys=100)
for obj in objects:
    print(obj["Key"], obj["Size"], obj["LastModified"])

# Lazily iterate over all objects under a prefix
for obj in store.iter_objects("my-bucket", prefix="logs/"):
    print(obj["Key"])

meta = store.head_object("my-bucket", "data/hello.txt")   # metadata only, no body
store.exists("my-bucket", "data/hello.txt")               # True / False

docs.title: Buckets and presigned URLs
docs.text:
store.bucket_exists("my-bucket")      # True / False
store.create_bucket("my-bucket")      # no-op if it already exists

url = store.presigned_url("my-bucket", "data/hello.txt", expires_in=3600)              # download URL
put_url = store.presigned_url("my-bucket", "uploads/new.bin", method="put_object")     # upload URL

docs.title: Custom Object Storage (MinIO, Ceph, …)
docs.text:
Pass the store's endpoint as endpoint_url. Most self-hosted stores also need path-style addressing:

store = S3Storage(
    access_key_id="your-key",
    secret_access_key="your-secret",
    region_name="us-east-1",
    endpoint_url="https://your-custom-object-store.local",
    use_path_style=True,
)

All methods work the same way against the custom endpoint.

docs.title: Agent Specification
docs.text:
This document defines the schema for describing an “Agent” (a Subject) — its identity, static deployment info, metadata, persona, prompting rules, execution policy, integrations (policies/tools/models/etc.), runtime resources, and governance.

The schema is implemented by the dataclasses in the subjects service (db/core/schema.py). Subjects are stored through the subjects API (POST /api/subjects, see Creating an Agent).

It’s designed for:

  • Declarative configuration (files, DB rows, or APIs)
  • Deterministic execution (stable defaults, explicit types)
  • Modularity (drop-in capabilities and subsystems)
  • Extensibility (safe addition of new items/sections)

docs.title: What this spec gives you
docs.text:
• Separation of concerns Identity vs. persona vs. policy vs. runtime resources vs. governance are cleanly scoped.
  • Composable capabilities Tools, functions, DSLs, models, memory systems, subsystems, and addons plug in uniformly.
  • Prompting ergonomics Consistent system/input/output templates and per-prompt overrides.
  • Execution safety Explicit logging level, code-execution toggle, and memory-class controls.
  • Runtime portability Per-replica resource profile, node selectors, and env for any orchestrator.
  • Governance & ownership Contact/owner metadata kept distinct for audits and approvals.

docs.title: Full agent specification structure
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Any, Literal


# ---------- Core ----------
@dataclass
class SubjectVersion:
    version: str
    release_tag: str


@dataclass
class OwnerInfo:
    org_id: Optional[str] = None
    org_name: Optional[str] = None
    team: Optional[str] = None
    owners: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)         # emails/user IDs
    contacts: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # {"slack":"...", "email":"..."}


@dataclass
class ResourceProfile:
    device: Literal["cpu", "gpu", "tpu"] = "cpu"
    cpu_cores: float = 1.0                # per replica
    memory_mb: int = 2048                 # per replica
    storage_mb: int = 0                   # per replica
    gpu_count: int = 0                    # per replica
    gpu_memory_mb: Optional[int] = None
    node_selector: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    env: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


# ---------- Capability items ----------
@dataclass
class ContractItem:
    contract_type: str
    contract_id: str
    contract_parameters: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass
class DSLItem:
    dsl_type: str
    dsl_workflow_id: str
    dsl_parameters: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass
class ModelItem:
    llm_type: str
    llm_block_id: str
    llm_selection_query: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Top-Level Layout
docs.text:
{
  "identity": { ... },
  "info": { ... },
  "metadata": { ... },
  "persona": { ... },
  "prompting": { ... },
  "execution": { ... },
  "integrations": { ... },
  "runtime": { ... },
  "owner": { ... }
}

Below, each section lists: Field, Type, Required?, Default, Description.

Payload rules (subjects API):

  • Every section is optional, but identity.subject_version (with both version and release_tag) must always be present. Without it the request fails.
  • Unknown fields inside a section are rejected: the section is built with Class(**data), so an unexpected key causes an error.
  • A null section value is not accepted; omit the section instead.

docs.title: 1) identity — SubjectIdentity
docs.text:
Field Type Required? Default Description subject_id str (set post-init) No — Unique ID of the subject. If omitted on create, the subjects service assigns a MongoDB ObjectId string. Used as the agent's SUBJECT_ID and as the id of workflow agent nodes. subject_name str No "" Human-friendly name for the agent. subject_type str No "" Category/class (e.g., "researcher", "assistant"). subject_version SubjectVersion No {"version":"0.1.0","release_tag":"dev"} Semver + release tag for this agent build.

SubjectVersion

Field Type Required? Default Description version str Yes — Semantic version (e.g., "1.2.3"). release_tag str Yes — Channel or label (e.g., "dev", "stable").

docs.title: 2) info — SubjectStaticInfo
docs.text: Field Type Required? Default Description container_image_name str No "" Container image of the agent. The deployer runs this image for every agent instance, so it is required before deploying the agent. static_env Dict[str,Any] No {} Static environment values for the agent. static_settings Dict[str,Any] No {} Static settings. static_parameters Dict[str,Any] No {} Static parameters. static_metadata Dict[str,Any] No {} Static metadata. container_registry_info str No "" Registry information (a string, not an object).

docs.title: 3) metadata — SubjectMetadata
docs.text: Field Type Required? Default Description subject_description str No "" Narrative description of the agent. subject_search_tags List[str] No [] Searchable tags for discovery. subject_traits List[str] No [] Behavioral traits (e.g., "concise", "formal"). subject_metadata Dict[str,str] No {} Freeform key-value metadata (small strings).

docs.title: 4) persona — AgentPersona
docs.text: Field Type Required? Default Description role str No "" The agent’s function/expertise. goal str No "" Primary objective guiding decisions. persona str No "" Backstory/narrative for tone and consistency. default_system_message str No "" Baseline system prompt; applied when no template overrides. config dict No {} Free-form persona configuration.

docs.title: 5) prompting — PromptingConfig & ManagementCommandItem
docs.text:
Field Type Required? Default Description default_system_template Optional[str] No None Jinja-like template for the system prompt. input_template Optional[str] No None Template for user/input formatting. output_template Optional[str] No None Template for agent outputs. prompts_config Dict[str,Any] No {} Named prompt snippets/vars for advanced setups.

ManagementCommandItem (used in runtime.management_commands or inside modules)

Field Type Required? Default Description command str Yes — Command name (e.g., "reset", "warmup"). command_description Optional[str] No None Human-friendly description. input_template Optional[str] No None Template for command input. output_template Optional[str] No None Template for command output.

docs.title: 6) execution — ExecutionPolicy
docs.text: Field Type Required? Default Description logging_level "CRITICAL" \| "ERROR" \| "WARNING" \| "INFO" \| "DEBUG" No "INFO" Runtime log verbosity. support_delegations bool No False Allow the agent to delegate tasks to other agents/tools. execute_code bool No False Permit code execution (use cautiously). enabled_memory_classes List[str] No [] Memory tiers the agent may use (e.g., ["short-term","long-term","context"]).

docs.title: 7) integrations — IntegrationConfig
docs.text:
This is the “plug-in board” for capabilities.

Field Type Required? Default Description policies List[PolicyItem] No [] Policies used by the agent executor (pre-check, rate limit, backlog, load balancing, autoscaling). dsls List[DSLItem] No [] Registered DSL workflows. models List[ModelItem] No [] Model/LLM backends and parameters. addons List[AddonItem] No [] Sidecar features (analytics, guards, etc.). contracts List[ContractItem] No [] Contract modules and parameters. subject_tools List[ToolItem] No [] Tools the agent can call (local/remote). subject_functions List[FunctionItem] No [] Functions callable by the agent (strong typing optional). memory_systems List[MemoryItem] No [] Memory providers (vector DBs, caches). sub_systems List[SubSystemItem] No [] External subsystems (routing, evaluators, schedulers). builtin_modules List[BuiltinModules] No [] First-class modules shipped with the platform.

PolicyItem

Field Type Required? Default Description policy_type str No "" Which executor hook the policy plugs into (see below). policy_rule_uri str No "" URI of the policy in the Policy DB. parameters Dict No {} Policy parameters. settings Dict No {} Policy settings.

The agent executor looks up these policy_type values (the first matching policy is used). A hook with no policy uses its built-in default.

policy_type Used by the executor for message_prechecker Accept/reject incoming tasks rate_limiter Per-session rate limiting message_backlog Deciding whether to backlog a task load_balancer Choosing which agent instance receives a task autoscaler Scaling agent instances up or down

DSLItem

Field Type Required? Default Description dsl_type str Yes — E.g., "graph", "dag". dsl_workflow_id str Yes — Registry/workflow identifier. dsl_parameters Dict[str,Any] No {} Runtime parameters / overrides.

ModelItem

Field Type Required? Default Description llm_type str Yes — Model family/type ("hf", "openai", etc.). llm_block_id str Yes — Concrete deployment or block id. llm_selection_query Dict[str,Any] No {} Query for dynamic model selection. llm_parameters Dict[str,Any] No {} Generation params (temperature, top_p, …).

AddonItem

Field Type Required? Default Description addon_id str Yes — Addon ID. addon_type str Yes — Addon kind (e.g., "guardrails", "analytics"). addon_config Dict[str,Any] No {} Configuration map.

ToolItem

Field Type Required? Default Description tool_id str Yes — Tool registry ID. tool_description str No "" Human-readable description. tool_execution_mode "local" \| "remote" No "local" Where the tool executes. tool_custom_config Dict[str,Any] No {} Tool-specific config (auth, timeouts, etc.). tool_calling_config Dict[str,Any] No {} Function-calling schema, arg hints, safety flags.

FunctionItem

Field Type Required? Default Description function_id str Yes — Function registry ID. function_custom_parameters Dict[str,Any] No {} Input defaults/overrides. function_calling_config Dict[str,Any] No {} JSON schema / arg mapping / safety.

MemoryItem

Field Type Required? Default Description memory_id str Yes — Memory system ID. memory_type str No "" Logical type ("short-term", "long-term", etc.). memory_backend str No "" Engine/driver (e.g., "weaviate", "redis"). memory_custom_config Dict[str,Any] No {} Index names, TTLs, dimensions, etc.

SubSystemItem

Field Type Required? Default Description sub_system_id str Yes — Subsystem ID. sub_system_type str No "" Category (router, evaluator, scheduler). sub_system_config Dict[str,Any] No {} Config map.

ContractItem

Field Type Required? Default Description contract_type str Yes — Contract class/kind. contract_id str Yes — Registry/deployment ID. contract_parameters Dict[str,Any] No {} Parameters for evaluation/execution.

BuiltinModules

Field Type Required? Default Description module_id str No "" Built-in module ID. module_description str No "" Description of functionality. module_input_template str No "" Input template for the module. module_output_template str No "" Output template for the module. module_management_commands List[ManagementCommandItem] No [] Module-scoped management commands.

docs.text:
Field Type Required? Default Description resources ResourceProfile No See defaults Per-replica compute/storage and scheduling hints. management_commands List[ManagementCommandItem] No [] Global management commands for this agent. exchanges List[str] No [] Job exchange IDs the agent registers with.

ResourceProfile

Field Type Required? Default Description device "cpu" \| "gpu" \| "tpu" No "cpu" Execution device type. cpu_cores float No 1.0 vCPU per replica. memory_mb int No 2048 Memory (MB) per replica. storage_mb int No 0 Ephemeral/storage (MB) per replica. gpu_count int No 0 GPUs per replica. gpu_memory_mb Optional[int] No None GPU memory hint (MB). node_selector Dict[str,str] No {} Scheduler affinity hints (labels). env Dict[str,str] No {} Environment variables for the process.

Default Description org_id Optional[str] No None Organization ID. org_name Optional[str] No None Organization name. team Optional[str] No None Team name/slug. owners List[str] No [] Owner user IDs/emails. contacts Dict[str,str] No {} Contact channels (e.g., "slack", "email").

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Agent sub-systems are modular components that extend an agent’s capabilities in a distributed AI environment. By integrating different sub-systems, agents can delegate tasks, plan and execute behaviors, verify results, collaborate via voting, exchange messages in real time, and even communicate directly with other agents over peer-to-peer connections.

These sub-systems can be selectively enabled and individually configured in the agent’s Subject Specification, allowing a tailored setup that matches the agent’s role and responsibilities. With them, we can achieve:

  • Scalable task delegation and orchestration
  • LLM-powered behavior planning and decision-making
  • Result verification workflows for quality control
  • Collaborative decision-making through voting systems
  • Real-time communication via chat and event streaming
  • Direct peer-to-peer communication without central brokers
Sub-System Name Purpose / Use Case Delegation System Allows an agent to delegate sub-tasks to other agents, track their execution status, and receive results. Supports REST APIs for CRUD operations and NATS for real-time task/result events. Behavior Controller Generates and executes structured behavior plans using LLMs in two phases (planning & selection). Supports context-aware reasoning, integrates with AIOS or OpenAI, and persists results for reuse. Verification System Manages verification workflows for delegated tasks, storing results in MongoDB, and broadcasting live status via WebSocket. Supports single-agent and multi-agent verification with NATS for ad-hoc checks. Social Choice & Voting System Coordinates collaborative decision-making among multiple agents using voting strategies (majority, weighted, etc.). Provides REST APIs for social tasks and NATS for real-time result streaming.

docs.title: Agents Task Delegation — Client Developer Documentation
Introduction
docs.text:
The Agents Task Delegation system allows one agent (the sender) to delegate sub-tasks to another agent (the target) in a distributed, event-driven environment. It provides:

  • REST APIs to create, update, query, and delete delegation records.
  • Status tracking for live workflow stages.
  • NATS-based real-time communication to send tasks and receive results.

A typical client workflow is:

  1. Create a delegation via REST API.
  2. Notify the target agent by publishing a delegation_task event on NATS.
  3. Track progress through REST queries or WebSocket updates.
  4. Submit results via REST or publish a delegation_result event.

docs.title: Registering Delegation System in Subject Specification
docs.text: The delegation system can be registered as a sub-module in an agent’s Subject Specification by adding an entry of type SubSystemItem. This configuration tells the agent where to reach the Delegations API, how to connect to the NATS messaging bus, and what defaults to apply when a delegation request does not specify all parameters.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
@dataclass
class SubSystemItem:
    sub_system_id: str
    sub_system_type: str = ""
    sub_system_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Minimal Required Configuration
docs.text:
Below is the minimal JSON block you need to include in the subject specification to enable the delegation system.

{
  "sub_system_id": "delegation-system-01",
  "sub_system_type": "delegation-system",
  "sub_system_config": {
    "api_base_url": "http://delegations-api.default.svc.cluster.local:8080/delegations",
    "nats_url": "nats://nats.default.svc.cluster.local:4222",
    "default_workflow_level": 1,
    "default_delegation_type": "manual",
    "default_deadline_seconds": 3600
  }
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text: Field Location Type Description sub_system_id root str Unique identifier for this subsystem entry in the subject spec. sub_system_type root str Must be "delegation-system" for the delegation sub-module. sub_system_config.api_base_url config str Base REST API URL for the Delegations service. All HTTP calls (create, update, query) will be sent here. sub_system_config.nats_url config str NATS server connection string used for sending and receiving real-time delegation events. sub_system_config.default_workflow_level config int Default workflow stage for delegations when none is specified in a request. sub_system_config.default_delegation_type config str Default delegation type (manual, system, auction, etc.) when not specified. sub_system_config.default_deadline_seconds config int Default allowed time (in seconds) before a delegated task expires.

docs.title: Example in a Subject Specification
docs.text:
If your Subject Specification is a JSON or YAML file that lists subsystems, you would add this as one entry in the sub_systems list:

{
  "subject_id": "agent-alpha",
  "subject_type": "agent",
  "sub_systems": [
    {
      "sub_system_id": "delegation-system-01",
      "sub_system_type": "delegation-system",
      "sub_system_config": {
        "api_base_url": "http://delegations-api.default.svc.cluster.local:8080/delegations",
        "nats_url": "nats://nats.default.svc.cluster.local:4222",
        "default_workflow_level": 1,
        "default_delegation_type": "manual",
        "default_deadline_seconds": 3600
      }
    }
  ]
}

This ensures that when the agent needs to delegate a sub-task, it knows exactly where to send the API requests and how to communicate over NATS for event-driven updates, with safe defaults for workflow level, delegation type, and deadlines.

docs.title: REST Client
docs.text:
You can use requests or any HTTP library of your choice.

import requests

BASE_URL = "http://<delegations-api-url>/delegations"

docs.title: NATS Client
docs.text:
Use the provided NATSAPI helper or nats-py directly.

from delegation_tasks_pusher import NATSAPI

nats = NATSAPI(nats_url="nats://localhost:4222")

docs.title: Creating a Delegation
docs.text:
payload = {
    "task_id": "task123",
    "sub_task_id": "sub456",
    "workflow_level": 1,
    "delegation_type": "manual",
    "target_subject_id": "agentB",
    "sender_subject_id": "agentA",
    "sub_task_data": {"param": "value"}
}

resp = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}", json=payload)
print(resp.json())

Expected Output:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Delegation created successfully"
}

docs.title: Sending a Delegation Event
docs.text:
nats.push_event(
    topic="agentB",
    sender_subject_id="agentA",
    event_type="delegation_task",
    event_data={
        "task_id": "task123",
        "sub_task_id": "sub456",
        "delegation_id": "del789",
        "data": {"info": "Execute this subtask"}
    }
)

docs.title: Listening for Delegation Events
docs.text:
import asyncio
import json
from nats.aio.client import Client as NATS

async def on_message(msg):
    data = json.loads(msg.data.decode())
    print(f"Received: {data}")

async def main():
    nc = NATS()
    await nc.connect("nats://localhost:4222")
    await nc.subscribe("agentB", cb=on_message)
    await asyncio.sleep(100)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Fetching a Delegation by ID
docs.text:
delegation_id = "del789"
resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/{delegation_id}")
print(resp.json())

docs.title: Querying Delegations
docs.text:
query_payload = {"target_subject_id": "agentB"}
resp = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/query", json=query_payload)
print(resp.json())

docs.title: Updating Delegation Status
docs.text:
status_payload = {
    "state": "in_progress",
    "time": 1717390000,
    "deadline": 1717400000
}
status_key = "execution"
delegation_id = "del789"

resp = requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/{delegation_id}/status/{status_key}", json=status_payload)
print(resp.json())

docs.title: Submitting Final Result
docs.text:
result_payload = {
    "state": "done",
    "delegation_result": "Execution completed successfully"
}

resp = requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/submit_result/del789", json=result_payload)
print(resp.json())

docs.title: Receiving Results via NATS
docs.text:
If the target agent uses NATS to send back a result:

nats.push_event(
    topic="agentA",
    sender_subject_id="agentB",
    event_type="delegation_result",
    event_data={
        "delegation_id": "del789",
        "result": "Execution completed successfully"
    }
)

docs.title: Deleting a Delegation
docs.text:
delegation_id = "del789"
resp = requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/{delegation_id}")
print(resp.json())

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The Behavior Controller is a two-phase reasoning and execution module that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to plan and select structured behaviors for an agent. It provides:

  • REST APIs for Phase 1 (behavior planning) and Phase 2 (behavior selection).
  • Context-aware processing by incorporating prior results or FrameDB pointers.
  • Multiple LLM backends (internal AIOS gRPC or external OpenAI API).
  • Persistent storage for all task data and results to allow auditing and reuse.

A typical client workflow is:

  1. Submit a Phase 1 request via REST API to generate a structured plan.
  2. Optionally reuse prior context for memory-aware planning.
  3. Submit a Phase 2 request with candidate behaviors to select the next action.
  4. Fetch results via REST API or database queries.

docs.title: Registering Behavior Controller in Subject Specification
docs.text: The Behavior Controller can be registered as a sub-module in an agent’s Subject Specification by adding an entry of type SubSystemItem. This configuration tells the agent where to reach the Behavior Controller API and what defaults to use for LLM execution.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
@dataclass
class SubSystemItem:
    sub_system_id: str
    sub_system_type: str = ""
    sub_system_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Minimal Required Configuration
docs.text:
Below is the minimal JSON block you need to include in the subject specification to enable the Behavior Controller.

{
  "sub_system_id": "behavior-controller-01",
  "sub_system_type": "behavior-controller",
  "sub_system_config": {
    "api_base_url": "http://behavior-controller.default.svc.cluster.local:8888",
    "llm_backend": "aios", 
    "default_phase1_template_id": "phase1-default",
    "default_phase2_template_id": "phase2-default"
  }
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text: Field Location Type Description sub_system_id root str Unique identifier for this subsystem entry in the subject spec. sub_system_type root str Must be "behavior-controller" for the behavior control sub-module. sub_system_config.api_base_url config str Base REST API URL for the Behavior Controller service. All HTTP calls (Phase 1 and Phase 2 processing) go here. sub_system_config.llm_backend config str LLM execution backend (aios for internal AIOS gRPC, openai for OpenAI API). sub_system_config.default_phase1_template_id config str ID of the default Phase 1 prompt template to use when none is specified. sub_system_config.default_phase2_template_id config str ID of the default Phase 2 prompt template to use when none is specified.

docs.title: Example in a Subject Specification
docs.text:
{
  "subject_id": "agent-beta",
  "subject_type": "agent",
  "sub_systems": [
    {
      "sub_system_id": "behavior-controller-01",
      "sub_system_type": "behavior-controller",
      "sub_system_config": {
        "api_base_url": "http://behavior-controller.default.svc.cluster.local:8888",
        "llm_backend": "aios",
        "default_phase1_template_id": "phase1-default",
        "default_phase2_template_id": "phase2-default"
      }
    }
  ]
}

This ensures that when the agent needs to plan or select behaviors, it knows exactly where to send API requests, which LLM backend to use, and which default templates to apply.

docs.title: REST Client
docs.text:
You can use requests or any HTTP client library.

import requests

BASE_URL = "http://<behavior-controller-api-url>"

docs.title: Submitting a Phase 1 Task (Behavior Planning)
docs.text:
payload = {
    "search_id": "task-001",
    "phase_1_data": {
        "input_description": "Plan a 3-step workflow to process satellite imagery."
    }
}

resp = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/process-phase-1-task", json=payload)
print(resp.json())

Expected Output:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "status": "success",
    "processed_data": {
      "plan": [
        {"task_id": "t1", "description": "Download images", "execution_type": "tool_call", "tool_id": "image_fetcher"},
        {"task_id": "t2", "description": "Preprocess images", "execution_type": "dsl", "dsl_id": "preprocess.dsl"},
        {"task_id": "t3", "description": "Run classification", "execution_type": "tool_call", "tool_id": "classifier"}
      ]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Submitting a Phase 2 Task (Behavior Selection)
docs.text:
payload = {
    "search_id": "task-001",
    "phase_2_data": {
        "planned_tasks": [
            {"task_id": "t1", "description": "Download images"},
            {"task_id": "t2", "description": "Preprocess images"},
            {"task_id": "t3", "description": "Run classification"}
        ]
    }
}

resp = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/process-phase-2-task", json=payload)
print(resp.json())

Expected Output:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "status": "success",
    "processed_data": {
      "uid": "t2"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Fetching Historical Phase 1 Results
docs.text:
resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/phase1-results/latest?limit=5")
print(resp.json())

docs.title: Example: Switching LLM Backend in Config
docs.text:
If you want to use OpenAI instead of AIOS:

{
  "sub_system_id": "behavior-controller-01",
  "sub_system_type": "behavior-controller",
  "sub_system_config": {
    "api_base_url": "http://behavior-controller.default.svc.cluster.local:8888",
    "llm_backend": "openai",
    "default_phase1_template_id": "phase1-default",
    "default_phase2_template_id": "phase2-default"
