docs.title: Social Choice & Voting System — Client Developer Documentation
Introduction
docs.text:
The Social Choice & Voting System coordinates collaborative decision-making among multiple agents. It provides:

  • REST APIs to create and manage social tasks (voting workflows).
  • NATS integration for receiving final voting results in real time.
  • Support for multiple voting strategies (e.g., majority, weighted).

A typical client workflow is:

  1. Create a social voting task via REST.
  2. Invite participants and define the goal data.
  3. Wait for voting completion via NATS.
  4. Retrieve and process the voting result.

docs.title: Registering Social Choice & Voting System in Subject Specification
docs.text: Add a SubSystemItem entry so the agent can connect to the social voting APIs and NATS result stream.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
@dataclass
class SubSystemItem:
    sub_system_id: str
    sub_system_type: str = ""
    sub_system_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Minimal Required Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "sub_system_id": "social-choice-voting-01",
  "sub_system_type": "social-choice-voting",
  "sub_system_config": {
    "api_base_url": "http://social-voting-api.default.svc.cluster.local:5001",
    "nats_url": "nats://nats.default.svc.cluster.local:4222"
  }
}

Fields

  • api_base_url – REST API base path for social task operations.
  • nats_url – NATS connection for streaming voting results.

docs.title: Import and Setup
docs.text:
from agent_sdk.verification import SocialTaskService

service = SocialTaskService("http://localhost:5001")

docs.title: Creating a Social Task
docs.text:
task = service.create_social_task(
    created_by_subject_id="agent_a",
    voting_type="majority",
    invited_subject_ids=["agent_b", "agent_c"],
    goal_data={"decision": "select_strategy"},
    status="pending",
    report={},
    voting_pqt_dsl_id="dsl_123",
    choice_evaluation_dsl="eval_dsl",
    deadline_time=1688888888
)

print("Created Social Task:", task.social_task_id)

docs.title: Waiting for Voting Result via NATS
docs.text:
waiter = service.create_waiter_for_task(task_id=task.social_task_id)
result = waiter.get()
print("Voting Result:", result.voting_result)

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The Verification System coordinates task verification workflows for agents, supporting both single-subject and multi-agent verification. It provides:

  • REST APIs for creating, updating, querying, and deleting verification tasks.
  • WebSocket server for live result updates.
  • NATS integration for ad-hoc verifications and social choice voting.

A typical client workflow is:

  1. Create a verification task via REST.
  2. Notify or invite agents over NATS.
  3. Wait for results via WebSocket or NATS.
  4. Submit verification results back to the system.

docs.title: Registering Verification System in Subject Specification
docs.text: Add a SubSystemItem entry to the subject spec so the agent knows how to reach the Verification API and connect to NATS for events.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
@dataclass
class SubSystemItem:
    sub_system_id: str
    sub_system_type: str = ""
    sub_system_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Minimal Required Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "sub_system_id": "verification-system-01",
  "sub_system_type": "verification-system",
  "sub_system_config": {
    "api_base_url": "http://verification-api.default.svc.cluster.local:5000/verifications",
    "nats_url": "nats://nats.default.svc.cluster.local:4222",
    "websocket_url": "ws://verification-api.default.svc.cluster.local:8765/ws"
  }
}

Fields

  • api_base_url – REST API base path for all verification endpoints.
  • nats_url – NATS connection for ad-hoc verifications/voting.
  • websocket_url – WebSocket endpoint for real-time verification status.

docs.title: Import and Setup
docs.text:
import requests
from agent_sdk.verification import VerificationClient, AdhocVerification

docs.title: Creating a Verification
docs.text:
client = VerificationClient("http://localhost:5000")
resp = client.create_verification(
    task_id="task_123",
    subject_id="agent_a",
    verification_type="manual"
)
print(resp)

docs.title: Submitting a Result
docs.text:
resp = requests.post(
    "http://localhost:5000/verifications/<verification_id>/submit-result",
    json={
        "target_subject_id": "agent_1",
        "status": "completed",
        "result_data": {
            "verification_result": {"pass": True},
            "verification_output": {"notes": "All checks passed"}
        }
    }
)
print(resp.json())

docs.title: Listening for Updates (WebSocket)
docs.text:
import asyncio, websockets

async def listen():
    async with websockets.connect("ws://localhost:8765/ws/agent_a/task_123") as ws:
        while True:
            msg = await ws.recv()
            print("Update:", msg)

asyncio.run(listen())

docs.title: Ad-hoc Verification via NATS
docs.text:
verifier = AdhocVerification("nats://localhost:4222")
verifier.push(
    subject="agent_a__task_123",
    event_type="start_verification",
    sender_subject_id="agent_b",
    event_data={"input": "data"}
)
verifier.close()

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The Functions & Tools subsystem provides a unified, LLM-friendly way to register, discover, and execute reusable capabilities in your agent stack.

It supports:

  • Spec-time registration of items that your runtime can resolve later
  • Local and remote execution backends
  • LLM discoverability via a searchable registry
  • Custom tooling with lifecycle hooks and admin commands

Important: FunctionItem, ToolItem, and BuiltinModules are spec-registration types only. They declare what exists and how to call it. Your runtime resolves and executes them.

docs.title: FunctionItem (spec registration)
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Any

@dataclass
class FunctionItem:
    function_id: str
    function_custom_parameters: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    function_calling_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
  • function_id: Unique logical name or URI (e.g., "math.add", "svc://billing.refund").
  • function_custom_parameters: Deployment-agnostic extras (defaults, constraints, tags).
  • function_calling_config: How to call it (protocol, endpoint, method, headers, timeout, auth refs).

docs.title: ToolItem (spec registration)
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal

@dataclass
class ToolItem:
    tool_id: str
    tool_description: str = ""
    tool_execution_mode: Literal["local", "remote"] = "local"
    tool_custom_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    tool_calling_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
  • tool_id: Unique logical name/URI.
  • tool_description: Human/LLM-facing description.
  • tool_execution_mode: "local" (Python executor) or "remote" (HTTP/gRPC/etc).
  • tool_custom_config: Deployment-agnostic extras (schemas, defaults).
  • tool_calling_config: Transport details for remote tools or constructor args for local tools.

docs.title: BuiltinModules (custom tool packs)
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List

@dataclass
class BuiltinModules:
    module_id: str = ""
    module_description: str = ""
    module_input_template: str = ""
    module_output_template: str = ""
    module_management_commands: List[ManagementCommandItem] = field(default_factory=list)

Use this to bundle predefined local tools with consistent I/O templates and admin commands.

docs.title: Runtime Architecture
docs.text: Component Purpose ToolsFunctionsRegistry In-memory registry + execution router for tools & functions. ToolExecutor (abstract) Base class for local tool logic with validate/deploy/execute. LocalCustomTool Adapter binding a ToolExecutor to a ToolItem. PredefinedToolExecutor Executes remote tools per tool_calling_config. PredefinedFunctionExecutor Executes remote functions per function_calling_config. ToolsRegistrySDK (optional) REST client to CRUD/search tools in an external Tools service.

docs.title: Minimal Subject Spec Example
docs.text:
{
  "subject_id": "agent-capabilities",
  "subject_type": "agent",
  "tools": [
    {
      "tool_id": "local.multiplier",
      "tool_description": "Multiply x by a factor",
      "tool_execution_mode": "local",
      "tool_custom_config": { "schema": { "input": {"x":"number","factor":"number"} } },
      "tool_calling_config": { "executor_class": "agents.tools.multiplier.MultiplierTool" }
    },
    {
      "tool_id": "remote.summarize",
      "tool_description": "Summarize text via HTTP service",
      "tool_execution_mode": "remote",
      "tool_calling_config": {
        "protocol": "http",
        "endpoint": "http://summary.svc.cluster.local:8080/summarize",
        "method": "POST",
        "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer ${RUNTIME_TOKEN}"},
        "timeout_s": 20
      }
    }
  ],
  "functions": [
    {
      "function_id": "math.add",
      "function_custom_parameters": {"max_terms": 10},
      "function_calling_config": {
        "protocol": "grpc",
        "endpoint": "dns:///math.svc:9000",
        "method": "Add",
        "timeout_s": 10
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: ToolExecutor interface
docs.text:
class ToolExecutor:
    def deploy(self): ...
    def validate_inputs(self, input_data: dict) -> bool: ...
    def execute(self, input_data: dict) -> dict: ...
    def execute_command(self, command_name: str, data: dict) -> dict: ...

docs.title: Example: local multiplier tool
docs.text:
# agents/tools/multiplier.py
from agent_sdk.tools import ToolExecutor

class MultiplierTool(ToolExecutor):
    def deploy(self):
        # preload assets if needed
        pass

    def validate_inputs(self, input_data):
        return isinstance(input_data.get("x"), (int, float)) and isinstance(input_data.get("factor"), (int, float))

    def execute(self, input_data):
        if not self.validate_inputs(input_data):
            raise ValueError("x and factor must be numbers")
        return {"result": input_data["x"] * input_data["factor"]}

docs.title: ToolsFunctionsRegistry — Core Usage
docs.text:
from agent_sdk.tools.registry import ToolsFunctionsRegistry
from agent_sdk.tools.local import LocalCustomTool

registry = ToolsFunctionsRegistry()

# Register LOCAL tool
tool_item = {
  "tool_id": "local.multiplier",
  "tool_execution_mode": "local",
  "tool_calling_config": { "executor_class": "agents.tools.multiplier.MultiplierTool" }
}
registry.add_local_tool(LocalCustomTool, tool_item)

# Register REMOTE tool
remote_tool_item = {
  "tool_id": "remote.summarize",
  "tool_execution_mode": "remote",
  "tool_calling_config": {
    "protocol": "http",
    "endpoint": "http://summary.svc:8080/summarize",
    "method": "POST",
    "timeout_s": 20
  }
}
registry.add_tool(remote_tool_item)  # handled by PredefinedToolExecutor

# Register REMOTE function
fn_item = {
  "function_id": "math.add",
  "function_calling_config": {
    "protocol": "grpc",
    "endpoint": "dns:///math.svc:9000",
    "method": "Add",
    "timeout_s": 10
  }
}
registry.add_function(fn_item)       # handled by PredefinedFunctionExecutor

# Execute
out1 = registry.execute_tool("local.multiplier", {"x": 6, "factor": 7})
out2 = registry.execute_tool("remote.summarize", {"text": "Long text..."})
out3 = registry.execute_function("math.add", {"numbers": [1, 2, 3]})

Routing rules

  • Tool with tool_execution_mode="local" → LocalCustomTool → your ToolExecutor.
  • Tool with tool_execution_mode="remote" → PredefinedToolExecutor (HTTP/gRPC/etc).
  • Functions always route through PredefinedFunctionExecutor unless you wrap them as tools.

docs.title: Calling Config Conventions
docs.text:
These are guidelines for *_calling_config. Your runtime may extend them.

HTTP (remote tool/function)

{
  "protocol": "http",
  "endpoint": "http://host:port/path",
  "method": "POST",
  "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer ${TOKEN}"},
  "timeout_s": 15,
  "retry": {"tries": 3, "backoff_s": 0.5},
  "input_mapping": {"text": "$.input"},
  "output_mapping": {"result": "$.data.summary"}
}

gRPC (remote function)

{
  "protocol": "grpc",
  "endpoint": "dns:///service.svc:9000",
  "method": "Package.Service/Method"  // or "Method" if your client binds service
}

Local (tool)

{
  "executor_class": "agents.tools.multiplier.MultiplierTool",
  "constructor_args": {"warmup": true}
}

docs.title: Searchable Representation (LLM Discovery)
docs.text:
searchable = registry.get_searchable_representation()

Each entry typically includes:

Field Description id Tool or function ID type "tool" or "function" description Human/LLM-readable description tags Keywords for ranking and filtering sub_type Domain category (e.g., nlp.summarize, math) runtime_type local, http, grpc, cli, etc. protocol_type http, grpc, python, etc. schema Input/output schema (OpenAPI/JSON Schema-like) examples Minimal call examples

This is designed for Planner / DSLPlanner selection flows.

docs.title: Built-in Modules (Custom Tool Packs)
docs.text:
Use BuiltinModules to ship a curated set of tools with consistent I/O and admin controls.

builtin = BuiltinModules(
  module_id="text.utils",
  module_description="Text utilities: normalize, extract, summarize",
  module_input_template='{"text": "string"}',
  module_output_template='{"result": "string"}',
  module_management_commands=[
    {"name": "warmup", "description": "Preload models"},
    {"name": "reindex", "description": "Rebuild local caches"}
  ]
)

registry.add_builtin_module(builtin)
registry.execute_tool("text.utils/summarize", {"text": "..."})
registry.execute_tool_command("text.utils/summarize", "warmup", {})

docs.title: Management & CRUD (optional external service)
docs.text:
If you use a Tools Service:

from agent_sdk.tools.sdk import ToolsRegistrySDK

sdk = ToolsRegistrySDK(base_url="http://tools-service")

sdk.create_tool({...})
meta = sdk.get_tool_by_id("remote.summarize")
sdk.update_tool("remote.summarize", {"tags": ["nlp","summary"]})
sdk.delete_tool("legacy.tool")
hits = sdk.execute_query("summary AND remote")

docs.title: Validation & Health
docs.text:
• Local tools should implement validate_inputs() and optionally deploy() (warmup).

  • Remote calls should support:

  • Timeouts & retries

  • Input/output mapping
  • Typed schema validation (pre/post)

Example health check:

registry.check_tool("remote.summarize")      # ping HTTP endpoint /health
registry.check_function("math.add")          # gRPC reflection or custom "Ping"

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Spec vs runtime: keep secrets out of spec; pass via env/secret refs at runtime.
  • Stable IDs: choose deterministic tool_id / function_id.
  • Schemas: define schema.input / schema.output for validation and LLM clarity.
  • Observability: record latency, error rate, payload size, backend, and retries.
  • LLM surfacing: keep tool_description concise, action-oriented, and tag-rich.
  • Idempotency: design functions/tools to be safe for retry.

docs.title: End-to-End Quickstart
docs.text:
# 1) Load spec (tools & functions array) and register
registry = ToolsFunctionsRegistry()

for t in spec["tools"]:
    if t.get("tool_execution_mode", "local") == "local":
        registry.add_local_tool(LocalCustomTool, t)
    else:
        registry.add_tool(t)

for f in spec["functions"]:
    registry.add_function(f)

# 2) Discover for LLM
for entry in registry.get_searchable_representation():
    print(entry["id"], entry.get("description"))

# 3) Execute
result_tool = registry.execute_tool("remote.summarize", {"text": "Hello world"})
result_fn   = registry.execute_function("math.add", {"numbers": [1, 2, 3]})

This gives you a clean separation between spec-time registration (FunctionItem, ToolItem, BuiltinModules) and runtime execution (registry routing, local executors, and remote invocations) with LLM-ready discovery built in.

docs.title: Vector Database Integration — Client Developer Documentation
Introduction
docs.text:
The Vector Database add-on gives agents one interface for storing and searching embeddings (semantic search, recommendation, retrieval-augmented generation). It is provided by the EmbeddingsSDK class in the agent_addons package.

Supported providers:

  • Weaviate (via the weaviate-client v3 weaviate.Client API)
  • Pinecone (serverless indexes)

EmbeddingsSDK provides:

  • Collection (Weaviate class / Pinecone index) management.
  • Vector CRUD and similarity search with metadata filters.
  • Text-based helpers that embed text with an embeddings generator before inserting or searching.
  • Ingestion of pre-computed vectors from local JSON/JSONL files or S3.

The same package includes AgentRAG, a small retrieval-augmented generation helper built on EmbeddingsSDK.

Typical workflow:

  1. Declare an AddonItem in the Subject Specification to record the vector DB (optional).
  2. Create an EmbeddingsSDK client for Weaviate or Pinecone.
  3. Create a collection, then insert vectors (or texts) with optional metadata.
  4. Search by vector or by text, with optional filters.
  5. Retrieve, update, or delete vectors as needed.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
EmbeddingsSDK is part of agent_addons (libs/agents-addons), which installs weaviate-client, pinecone-client and boto3.

pip install ./libs/agents-addons

docs.title: Registering Vector DB in Subject Specification
docs.text: Vector databases can be recorded in the subject's integrations.addons list using AddonItem.

docs.title: Data Class Reference
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Any

@dataclass
class AddonItem:
    addon_id: str
    addon_type: str
    addon_config: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "addon_id": "vector-primary",
  "addon_type": "vector_db",
  "addon_config": {
    "provider": "weaviate",
    "weaviate_url": "http://weaviate.default.svc.cluster.local:8080",
    "metric": "cosine"
  }
}

docs.title: Field Descriptions
docs.text:
Field Type Description addon_id str Unique identifier for this add-on. addon_type str Add-on kind, e.g. "vector_db". addon_config Dict[str, Any] Client settings. Use the EmbeddingsSDK constructor arguments as keys (see below).

The agents SDK does not create clients from add-on entries automatically. Read the entry from self.subject.integrations.addons in your agent and build the client yourself, e.g. EmbeddingsSDK(**addon.addon_config).

docs.title: Import and Setup
docs.text: from agent_addons.embeddings_store import EmbeddingsSDK

docs.title: Weaviate
docs.text:
vdb = EmbeddingsSDK(
    provider="weaviate",
    weaviate_url="http://localhost:8080",
    weaviate_api_key=None,      # optional
    metric="cosine",
)

docs.title: Pinecone
docs.text:
vdb = EmbeddingsSDK(
    provider="pinecone",
    pinecone_api_key="pc-...",
    dimension=1536,             # required to create indexes
    metric="cosine",
    pinecone_cloud="aws",
    pinecone_region="us-east-1",
)
Argument Default Description provider — (required) "weaviate" or "pinecone" (anything else raises ValueError) dimension None Vector dimension (used when creating Pinecone indexes) metric "cosine" Distance metric (Weaviate class distance / Pinecone index metric) weaviate_url None Required for Weaviate weaviate_api_key None Optional Weaviate API key pinecone_api_key None Required for Pinecone pinecone_index_name None Stored on the client for reference pinecone_cloud "aws" Serverless cloud for new indexes pinecone_region "us-east-1" Serverless region for new indexes

docs.title: A. Collections
docs.text:
A collection is a Weaviate class or a Pinecone index.

vdb.create_collection("KnowledgeBase")
vdb.list_collections()            # ['KnowledgeBase', ...]
vdb.delete_collection("KnowledgeBase")
  • Weaviate: creates a class with vectorizer: "none" (you bring your own embeddings), an HNSW index and the configured distance.
  • Pinecone: creates a serverless index with dimension and metric.

docs.title: B. Insert vectors
docs.text:
vdb.insert_vectors("KnowledgeBase", [
    {"id": "4b7c1c1e-6a8e-4b6c-9a0e-2f1a3b4c5d6e", "values": [0.12, 0.98, ...], "metadata": {"text": "Doc A", "source": "wiki"}},
    {"id": "9f0e2d3c-1b2a-4c5d-8e7f-6a5b4c3d2e1f", "values": [0.33, 0.71, ...]},
])
  • Weaviate: objects are batch-added with the given id as UUID (Weaviate requires UUIDs), values as the vector and metadata as properties.
  • Pinecone: the list is upserted as-is into the index.

docs.title: C. Get, update and delete
docs.text:
vdb.get_vector("KnowledgeBase", vid)                    # Weaviate object / Pinecone fetch result (dict)
vdb.update_vector("KnowledgeBase", vid, new_values, metadata={"source": "updated"})
vdb.delete_vector("KnowledgeBase", vid)

docs.title: D. Similarity search
docs.text:
results = vdb.search("KnowledgeBase", query_vector, top_k=5, filters=None)

filters is passed to the provider unchanged:

  • Weaviate: a where filter, e.g. {"path": ["source"], "operator": "Equal", "valueText": "wiki"}. The result is the raw GraphQL response ({"data": {"Get": {"KnowledgeBase": [...]}}}).
  • Pinecone: a metadata filter, e.g. {"source": {"$eq": "wiki"}}. The result is the raw query response (matches with id, score, metadata).

docs.title: E. Text-based helpers
docs.text:
These helpers take an embedder: any object with embed_texts(texts, batch_size=...) -> List[List[float]], such as the generators from the Embeddings SDK.

from agents_embeddings.custom import OpenAIEmbeddingsGenerator

embedder = OpenAIEmbeddingsGenerator(model="text-embedding-3-small")   # uses OPENAI_API_KEY

# Items can be strings or dicts with "text" (+ optional "id", "metadata")
vdb.insert_texts("KnowledgeBase", [
    "AI is transforming industries.",
    {"id": "4b7c1c1e-...", "text": "Vector DBs store embeddings.", "metadata": {"source": "notes"}},
], embedder=embedder, batch_size=128)

vdb.update_texts("KnowledgeBase", [{"id": "4b7c1c1e-...", "text": "Updated text"}], embedder=embedder)

hits = vdb.search_text("KnowledgeBase", "What stores embeddings?", embedder=embedder, top_k=3)

many = vdb.bulk_search_texts("KnowledgeBase", ["query one", "query two"], embedder=embedder, top_k=3)
  • Items without an id get a random hex ID (uuid4().hex).
  • insert_texts stores only the item's metadata, not the text itself. Include the text in metadata if you need it back from search results.
  • Use id_key, text_key and metadata_key to map other field names, and preprocess to transform text before embedding.

docs.title: F. Ingest pre-computed vectors
docs.text:
The file or S3 object must be a JSON array or JSONL of {"id", "values", "metadata"} records (or anything transform turns into that).

vdb.ingest_from_file("KnowledgeBase", "/data/vectors.jsonl", batch_size=100)

vdb.ingest_from_s3("KnowledgeBase", bucket="my-bucket", key="vectors/part-0001.jsonl",
                   region="us-east-1", transform=lambda r: {"id": r["uuid"], "values": r["emb"], "metadata": r["meta"]})

S3 ingestion uses the default boto3 credential chain; the region defaults to AWS_REGION.

docs.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (AgentRAG)
docs.text:
AgentRAG combines an EmbeddingsSDK, an embedder and an LLM to answer questions from stored documents.

from agent_addons.rag import AgentRAG
from agents_llm_lite.custom import OpenAIInference

llm = OpenAIInference(model="gpt-4o-mini")

rag = AgentRAG(
    collection="KnowledgeBase",
    embeddings_sdk=vdb,
    embedder=embedder,
    llm=llm,                     # an agents_llm_lite provider, e.g. OpenAIInference(model="gpt-4o-mini")
    text_field="text",           # metadata field holding the chunk text
    default_top_k=5,
    max_context_chars=12_000,
    chunk_size=1200,
    chunk_overlap=200,
)

rag.add_texts(["Acme was founded in 1999.", {"text": "RetailCo is based in Delaware."}])
rag.add_documents_chunked([{"id": "contract-1", "text": long_contract_text, "metadata": {"type": "contract"}}])

chunks = rag.retrieve("Where is RetailCo based?", top_k=3)   # List[RetrievedChunk(id, score, metadata, text)]

result = rag.ask("Where is RetailCo based?")
print(result["answer"])
print(result["sources"])      # chunks that fit in the context budget
  • add_texts and add_documents_chunked store the text in metadata[text_field], so it is available at retrieval time. Chunk IDs are <doc id>__0000, <doc id>__0001, …, and each chunk's metadata includes chunk_index and parent_id.
  • retrieve normalizes Weaviate and Pinecone results into RetrievedChunk objects, sorted by score (higher is better). Weaviate distances are converted to 1 / (1 + distance).
  • ask packs retrieved chunks into the prompt up to max_context_chars, asks the LLM to cite them as [1], [2], … (cite_inline=True), and returns {"answer", "sources", "retrieved"}. Pass prompt_template (with {context} and {question}) to customize the prompt, and callback to extract the answer text from your LLM's response (default: OpenAI choices[0].message.content).

docs.title: Advanced Agent Memories
docs.text:
Advanced Agent Memories (the MemoryGrid stack) gives agents long-term memory and a way to learn from it. Agents can:

  • remember what happened, what is true, how to do things, what they learned, and what worked;
  • mine lessons from that experience on a schedule;
  • have humans review those lessons before they are trusted;
  • apply the trusted lessons when solving new tasks; and
  • track whether applied lessons actually helped, retiring the ones that keep failing.

This section documents the agent-memories codebase, which contains four Python packages and the Kubernetes manifests for their databases.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Package / service What it does Docs Agentic Memory agentic_memory (library) Six memory types — episodic, semantic, procedural, reflective, reward and session context — stored across PostgreSQL, Weaviate, ArangoDB and Redis behind one AgentMemory façade Agentic Memory Agent FS agent_fs (library) A git-backed, version-controlled file system per agent: read/write files, commit, branch, tag, diff, restore, revert, stash Agent FS Learner memorygrid_learner (FastAPI service) Mines lessons from agent experience, accepts injected lessons, enriches them, runs human review, and promotes approved lessons into a Skills store or Knowledge Base (git-versioned) Learner Incorporator & Feedback memorygrid_incorporator (FastAPI service) At task time, matches the current problem to a promoted lesson, turns it into a concrete action, records feedback, and escalates lessons that keep failing Incorporator & Feedback

docs.title: Memory types at a glance
docs.text: Type Question answered Store Docs Episodic What happened? mem.episodic Episodic Semantic What is true? mem.semantic Semantic Procedural How do I do this? mem.procedural Procedural Reflective What did I learn? mem.reflective Reflective Reward What works best? mem.reward Reward Context KV What is my current session state? mem.context_kv Context KV

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Download Image

The design has three core processes on top of the storage layer:

  1. Memory Manager (Process 1) — turns raw input into memory documents and places them in a knowledge graph.
  2. Learner (Process 2) — mines lessons from experience and graduates them through human review.
  3. Incorporator & Feedback (Process 3) — applies lessons at task time and feeds results back.

docs.title: Memory lifecycle
docs.text:
Download Image

  1. Execution & capture — the agent executes a task and records episodes (Agentic Memory).
  2. Memory processing — memories are summarized, tagged and placed in a graph (Memory Manager — design only).
  3. Learning — the Learner collects experience, extracts patterns, writes a lesson, enriches it, and sends it to human review. Approved lessons are promoted to the Skills DB or the Knowledge Base.
  4. Incorporation — at the next task, the Incorporator matches the task to a promoted lesson and returns a concrete action.
  5. Feedback loop — the outcome is recorded. A lesson that fails too often is sent back to human review and/or disabled.

docs.title: Implementation status
docs.text:
The diagrams describe the complete target design. What the code implements today:

Design element Status Memory types (episodic, semantic, procedural, reflective, reward, context cache) Implemented — agentic_memory Git-versioned filesystem Implemented — agent_fs, plus the Learner's own lessons repository Learner Process: trigger, data collection, pattern extraction, lesson creation, watcher, enrichment, human review, promotion, cross-agent sharing, metrics Implemented — memorygrid_learner Incorporator: plug-in API, DSL/LLM matching, DSL/LLM applier, feedback DB, threshold escalation (human/auto paths), metrics Implemented — memorygrid_incorporator Memory Manager (memory document creator, metadata generator, grapher) Design only (diagram) Team/org-level memory scopes, CRDT concurrent-write layer, shared workspace/blackboard/consensus (diagram) Design only FrameDB SDK (Redis/TiDB FrameDB via gRPC) Not used by this code. The Learner talks to TiDB (or SQLite) directly through SQLAlchemy Working memory, world model, strategic memory types Design only

Other diagrams: Memory storage · Learner process · Feedback.

docs.title: How the pieces connect
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────── agent runtime ───────────────────────────┐
                         │                                                                       │
  task ─► Incorporator /invoke ──► action ──► agent executes ──► Incorporator /outcome           │
                │                                   │                     │                      │
                │ match against                     │ remember_episode()   │ failures ≥ X         │
                ▼                                   ▼                     ▼                      │
     Skills DB / Knowledge Base ◄── promote ── Learner ◄── collect ── Agentic Memory     re-review / disable
     (TiDB + vector + git)             ▲                                                         │
                                       └── human review (approve / edit / reject) ◄──────────────┘
  • The Learner and the Incorporator share the same Skills/Knowledge Base storage. The Incorporator imports the Learner package and builds its storage objects from the same settings.
  • Agentic Memory is the long-term memory library the agent uses directly. The Learner's data collection currently uses in-process demo sources. See Learner → Feeding experience into the Learner for how to connect them.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Deploy the databases for Agentic Memory: Deployment.

  2. Give your agent memory:

    ```python from agentic_memory import AgentMemory, MemoryConfig from agentic_memory.models import Outcome

    with AgentMemory(MemoryConfig()) as mem: ep = mem.remember_episode("Retried the upload with backoff and it succeeded", session_id="s1", agent_id="uploader", outcome=Outcome.SUCCESS) mem.reflect("Backoff fixes transient upload errors", lesson="Retry uploads with exponential backoff", source_episode_id=ep.id) print(mem.recall("upload failures")) ```

  3. Run the Learner and the Incorporator services, and connect your agent pipeline to them: End-to-End Example.

docs.text:

    • Procedural Memory

    • Reward Memory
    • Context KV Memory
  • Agent FS — git-backed agent file system

  • End-to-End Example — the full learn → apply → feedback loop

docs.title: Agent FS
docs.text:
agent_fs gives each agent its own version-controlled file system, backed by a git repository. Every write can be committed automatically, so the agent's files have a full history. The agent can diff, restore, revert, branch, tag and stash, just like a developer working with git.

Typical uses:

  • a durable, auditable workspace for an agent's notes, plans, generated code or documents;
  • letting an agent experiment on a branch and merge only what works;
  • rolling a file back to the version that was known to be good.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
agent_fs is pure Python with no dependencies; it shells out to the git command-line tool, which must be installed. Requires Python ≥ 3.10.

The package lives in agent-memories/fs. Its pyproject.toml refers to a README.md that is not in the folder and uses an unusual build backend, so pip install may fail. In that case, put the folder on PYTHONPATH:

export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/path/to/agent-memories/fs

from agent_fs import AgentFS

docs.title: Creating a File System
docs.text:
fs = AgentFS("/var/lib/agents", subject_id="planner-agent",
             author_name="Planner Agent", author_email="planner@agents.local")
  • The root is <path>/<subject_id> (here /var/lib/agents/planner-agent). It is created if missing.
  • On first use, a git repository is initialised there with an empty initial commit, so HEAD is always valid.
  • All paths passed to the API are relative to that root. A path that resolves outside the root (for example ../other-agent/x) raises AgentFSError.

docs.title: Working with Files
docs.text:
sha = fs.write("notes/plan.md", "# Plan\n- step 1\n")          # writes and commits
fs.write("notes/plan.md", "# Plan\n- step 1\n- step 2\n", message="add step 2")
fs.write("data/blob.bin", b"\x00\x01", auto_commit=False)      # write without committing

fs.read("notes/plan.md")            # str (UTF-8)
fs.read_bytes("data/blob.bin")      # bytes

fs.copy("notes/plan.md", "notes/plan-v2.md")
fs.move("notes/plan-v2.md", "archive/plan-v2.md")
fs.delete("archive/plan-v2.md")

fs.mkdir("reports/2026")
fs.exists("notes/plan.md")          # True
fs.is_dir("reports")                # True
fs.list()                           # top-level entries (excluding .git)
fs.list("notes", recursive=True)    # depth-first listing

write, delete, move and copy commit by default, returning the new commit hash. The default messages are write: <path>, delete: <path>, move: <src> -> <dst> and copy: <src> -> <dst>. Pass auto_commit=False to batch several changes into one commit:

fs.write("a.txt", "A", auto_commit=False)
fs.write("b.txt", "B", auto_commit=False)
fs.stage()                          # git add -A (or fs.stage("a.txt", "b.txt"))
fs.commit("add a and b")

Missing files raise AgentFSFileNotFoundError.

docs.title: History and Diffs
docs.text:
fs.head()                                   # current commit hash
for c in fs.log(limit=5):                   # newest first
    print(c.short_hash, c.date, c.message, c.files_changed)
fs.log(file_path="notes/plan.md")           # commits touching one file
fs.log(branch="experiment")

fs.status()                                 # [StatusEntry(path, staged, unstaged), ...]

fs.diff()                                   # unstaged changes
fs.diff(staged=True)                        # staged changes
fs.diff(from_ref="HEAD~1")                  # HEAD~1 vs HEAD
fs.diff(from_ref="main", to_ref="experiment", file_path="notes/plan.md")

CommitInfo has hash, short_hash, author, email, date, message and files_changed.

docs.title: Restoring and Undoing
docs.text:
old = fs.read_at("notes/plan.md", "HEAD~2")      # content at any commit/branch/tag
raw = fs.read_bytes_at("data/blob.bin", "v1")

fs.restore("notes/plan.md", "HEAD~2")            # write the old content back (and commit)
fs.revert(commit_hash)                           # new commit undoing a commit
fs.cherry_pick(commit_hash)                      # apply a commit onto the current branch
fs.checkout("HEAD~1", file_path="notes/plan.md") # restore one file in the working tree

docs.title: Branches, Merges and Tags
docs.text:
fs.create_branch("experiment")                   # from HEAD (or from_ref="v1")
fs.checkout("experiment")
fs.write("notes/plan.md", "# Experimental plan\n")
fs.checkout("master")                            # the default branch name depends on your git config
fs.merge("experiment", message="merge experiment")
fs.delete_branch("experiment")                   # force=True for unmerged branches

fs.branches()                                    # ["experiment", "master"]
fs.current_branch()
fs.checkout("hotfix", create=True)               # create and switch

fs.tag("v1")                                     # lightweight tag
fs.tag("v2", message="known-good plan")          # annotated tag
fs.tags()                                        # newest first
fs.delete_tag("v1")

merge raises MergeConflictError on conflicts. Branch errors raise BranchError, and an unknown ref passed to checkout raises RefNotFoundError.

docs.title: Stash
docs.text:
fs.write("notes/wip.md", "half done", auto_commit=False)
fs.stage("notes/wip.md")   # new files must be staged; git stash ignores untracked files
fs.stash("work in progress")
fs.stash_list()        # [{"index": 0, "ref": "stash@{0}", "message": "On master: work in progress"}]
fs.stash_apply(0)      # apply, keep the entry
fs.stash_pop(0)        # apply and remove
fs.stash_drop(0)       # remove without applying

docs.title: Repository Summary
docs.text:
fs.info()
# {"root": "...", "branch": "master", "head": "...", "branches": [...], "tags": [...], "status": [...]}

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
All errors derive from AgentFSError:

Exception Raised when AgentFSFileNotFoundError A file to read, delete, move or copy does not exist CommitError A commit, revert or cherry-pick fails BranchError Creating or deleting a branch fails MergeConflictError A merge has conflicts RefNotFoundError A ref or path at a ref does not exist AgentFSError Any other git failure, or a path that escapes the root

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Area Methods Files read, read_bytes, write, delete, move, copy, mkdir, exists, is_dir, list Commits stage, unstage, commit, head, status, log, diff Branches branches, current_branch, create_branch, delete_branch, checkout, merge Tags tag, tags, delete_tag Versions read_at, read_bytes_at, restore, revert, cherry_pick Stash stash, stash_pop, stash_apply, stash_drop, stash_list Info info

docs.title: Agentic Memory
docs.text:
agentic_memory is a Python library that gives an agent six kinds of memory behind one façade, AgentMemory:

Store Model Backends mem.episodic EpisodicMemory PostgreSQL + Weaviate + ArangoDB mem.semantic SemanticMemory PostgreSQL + Weaviate + ArangoDB (knowledge graph) mem.procedural ProceduralMemory PostgreSQL + Weaviate + ArangoDB mem.reflective ReflectiveMemory PostgreSQL + Weaviate + ArangoDB mem.reward RewardMemory PostgreSQL + Weaviate + ArangoDB mem.context_kv plain dicts Redis

docs.title: How Storage Works
docs.text:
Every write to one of the five long-term types goes to three backends at once:

store(memory)
     │
     ├──► PostgreSQL   structured fields, exact lookups, filters, aggregates
     ├──► Weaviate     embedding vector (cosine similarity search)
     └──► ArangoDB     graph node (+ edges for relationships)

Reads use the most suitable backend:

Operation Backend retrieve(id), filters, aggregates PostgreSQL search(query) Weaviate finds the nearest IDs, then each record is loaded from PostgreSQL. score = 1 − cosine distance Relationships (links, paths, neighbours, provenance) ArangoDB traversal

Context KV is different: it lives only in Redis (one hash per agent session).

Writes are not transactional across backends. If one backend fails mid-write, the others may already hold the record.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Requires Python ≥ 3.8 and the four databases (see Deployment).

cd agent-memories/agentic-memory
pip install -e ".[dev]"

Dependencies: weaviate-client>=4.0, python-arango>=8.0, psycopg2>=2.9, openai>=1.0, redis>=5.0.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
from agentic_memory import (
    AgentMemory, MemoryConfig, PostgresConfig, WeaviateConfig, ArangoConfig, RedisConfig,
)

config = MemoryConfig(
    postgres=PostgresConfig(host="db.example.org", port=30432, database="agent_memory",
                            username="postgres", password="..."),
    weaviate=WeaviateConfig(host="db.example.org", port=30880, grpc_port=30851,
                            collection_prefix="AgentMemory", embedding_dim=1536),
    arango=ArangoConfig(url="http://db.example.org:30529", username="root",
                        password="...", database="agent_memory"),
    redis=RedisConfig(host="db.example.org", port=30637, password="...", db=0),
    embedding_model="text-embedding-3-small",
    top_k=5,
)
mem = AgentMemory(config)
Config Field Default PostgresConfig host, port, database, username, password localhost, 5432, agent_memory, postgres, "" WeaviateConfig host, port, grpc_port localhost, 8080, 50051 collection_prefix AgentMemory (collections AgentMemoryEpisodic, AgentMemorySemantic, …) embedding_dim 1536 (passed to the embedding provider) ArangoConfig url, username, password, database http://localhost:8529, root, "", agent_memory RedisConfig host, port, password, db localhost, 6379, "", 0 MemoryConfig embedding_model text-embedding-3-small top_k 5 (stored on the config; search methods take their own top_k)

AgentMemory() with no arguments connects to all four databases on localhost with default ports.

On start-up the library creates what it needs:

  • PostgreSQL tables and indexes (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS).
  • One Weaviate collection per memory type (HNSW index, cosine distance, no vectorizer).
  • The ArangoDB database plus its node and edge collections.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
Vectors come from an EmbeddingProvider. By default it calls the OpenAI embeddings API (text-embedding-3-small) and reads OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment.

from agentic_memory.embeddings import EmbeddingProvider

# Default: OpenAI
mem = AgentMemory(config, openai_api_key="sk-...")       # or set OPENAI_API_KEY

# Explicit provider
embedder = EmbeddingProvider(model="text-embedding-3-large", dim=3072, api_key="sk-...")
mem = AgentMemory(config, embedder=embedder)

# Any embedding function
def my_embed(text: str) -> list[float]:
    ...
mem = AgentMemory(config, embedder=EmbeddingProvider(embed_fn=my_embed, dim=768))

EmbeddingProvider provides embed(text) and embed_batch(texts). Use the same model (and dimension) for the lifetime of a Weaviate collection, because vectors from different models are not comparable.

What gets embedded for each type:

Type Embedded text Episodic content Semantic "{subject} {predicate} {object} {content}" Procedural "{name} {description} {step.action step.expected_outcome …}" Reflective "{content} {lesson} {improvement_suggestion}" Reward "{state_description} {action} {outcome}"

docs.title: Write helpers
docs.text:
from agentic_memory.models import Outcome

ep = mem.remember_episode(
    "User asked about the weather in Paris",
    session_id="sess-001", agent_id="weather-agent",
    context={"user": "alice", "channel": "chat"},
    outcome=Outcome.SUCCESS, importance=0.8, metadata={"lang": "en"},
)

fact = mem.know_fact("Paris", "is_capital_of", "France", confidence=1.0, source="wikipedia")

proc = mem.learn_procedure(
    "send_email",
    steps=[
        {"action": "compose", "parameters": {"to": "..."}, "expected_outcome": "draft ready"},
        {"action": "send", "parameters": {}, "expected_outcome": "email sent"},
    ],
    description="Send an email to a contact",
    trigger_conditions=["user wants to send an email"],
)

ref = mem.reflect(
    "I should confirm location before giving weather",
    lesson="Clarify ambiguous location references",
    improvement_suggestion="Ask 'Which Paris?' when unclear",
    source_episode_id=ep.id, confidence=0.9,
)

rw = mem.record_reward("low battery warning shown", "recharge_now", reward=1.0,
                       outcome="battery restored", policy="energy")
Method Returns Notes remember_episode(content, *, session_id, agent_id, context, outcome, importance, metadata) EpisodicMemory outcome defaults to Outcome.UNKNOWN, importance to 0.5 know_fact(subject, predicate, object_, *, content, confidence, source, metadata) SemanticMemory content defaults to "subject predicate object" learn_procedure(name, steps, *, description, trigger_conditions, metadata) ProceduralMemory steps are dicts with action, parameters, expected_outcome; step_order follows list order reflect(content, lesson, *, improvement_suggestion, source_episode_id, confidence, metadata) ReflectiveMemory Linking to an episode creates a provenance edge record_reward(state_description, action, reward, *, outcome, policy, context, metadata) RewardMemory policy defaults to "default"

Each helper builds the model and calls the store's store(). You can also build models yourself and call mem.<type>.store(memory).

docs.title: Searching everything: recall
docs.text:
results = mem.recall("weather questions", top_k=5)
# {"episodic": [...], "semantic": [...], "procedural": [...], "reflective": [...], "reward": [...]}

results = mem.recall("step", top_k=5, agent_id="planner-agent", session_id="session-99")
# ... plus "context": [{"key": "...", "value": {...}}, ...]

recall runs a vector search on each of the five long-term types. When agent_id or session_id is given, it also adds a "context" list: the session's context entries whose key or value contains the query string (case-insensitive substring match, up to top_k).

docs.title: Context helpers
docs.text:
mem.set_context("status", {"ready": True}, agent_id="planner", session_id="s1", ttl_seconds=600)
mem.get_context("status", agent_id="planner", session_id="s1")   # {"ready": True}

These are shorthands for mem.context_kv.set(...) / .get(...). See Context KV Memory.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
with AgentMemory(config) as mem:   # closes PostgreSQL, Weaviate and Redis on exit
    ...

mem = AgentMemory(config)
mem.close()

docs.title: Common Store Interface
docs.text:
Every long-term store (episodic, semantic, procedural, reflective, reward) implements:

Method Description store(memory) -> str Write to PostgreSQL, Weaviate and ArangoDB; returns the memory ID retrieve(memory_id) Load by ID from PostgreSQL (None if missing) search(query, top_k=5) Vector search; results carry .score (higher is more similar) update(memory) Re-embed and overwrite in all three backends delete(memory_id) Remove from all three backends (graph edges are not removed)

All models share the BaseMemory fields:

Field Type Default id str random UUID content str "" metadata dict {} embedding list[float] \| None set on store/update created_at datetime datetime.utcnow() score float \| None set by search

Enums: MemoryType (episodic, semantic, procedural, reflective, reward) and Outcome (success, failure, neutral, unknown).

docs.title: PostgreSQL tables
docs.text:
Table Holds Indexed columns episodic_memories episodes session_id, agent_id, outcome semantic_memories triples subject, predicate procedures procedures name procedure_steps steps (FK → procedures, cascade delete) procedure_id reflective_memories reflections source_episode_id reward_memories reward tuples action, policy

context, metadata, trigger_conditions and parameters are stored as JSONB.

docs.title: Weaviate collections
docs.text: <prefix>Episodic, <prefix>Semantic, <prefix>Procedural, <prefix>Reflective, <prefix>Reward. Each object has the memory's ID as its UUID, a memory_id property and the embedding vector.

docs.title: ArangoDB collections
docs.text: Collection Kind Contents episodic_nodes, semantic_nodes, procedural_nodes, reflective_nodes, reward_nodes vertex One node per memory (_key = memory ID) with its main fields entity_nodes vertex Knowledge-graph entities (one per distinct subject/object) memory_relations edge Episode ↔ episode links, reward state transitions entity_relations edge Subject → object edges of semantic facts (predicate, memory_id, confidence) episode_reflection edge Episode → reflection provenance

docs.title: Redis
docs.text: One hash per session: key <agent_id>__<session_id>, one field per context key, values stored as JSON.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
cd agent-memories/agentic-memory
pytest

The tests mock all four backends and do not need running databases. Runnable examples against real databases are in agent-memories/examples/ (example_episodic.py, example_semantic.py, example_procedural.py, example_reflective.py, example_reward.py, example_context_kv.py, example_openai_embeddings.py). Connection settings come from environment variables read by examples/db_config.py (POSTGRES_HOST, WEAVIATE_HOST, ARANGO_URL, REDIS_HOST, …).

docs.title: Context KV Memory
docs.text:
Context KV memory answers "what is my current session state?" It is a fast, schema-free key-value store for working state that belongs to one agent session: user preferences, task progress, scratch notes, tool-call counters.

It is backed by Redis hashes. Each (agent_id, session_id) pair is one hash, keyed <agent_id>__<session_id>, so:

  • all keys of a session can be listed, exported or wiped together;
  • a TTL applies to the whole session at once.

Values must be JSON-serializable. They are stored as JSON and returned as Python objects.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
from agentic_memory import AgentMemory

with AgentMemory(config) as mem:
    kv = mem.context_kv                     # ContextKVMemory bound to the configured Redis

Or standalone, without the other databases:

from agentic_memory.backends.redis_client import RedisClient
from agentic_memory.config import RedisConfig
from agentic_memory.memory_types.context_kv import ContextKVMemory

redis = RedisClient(RedisConfig(host="localhost", port=6379, password=""))
kv = ContextKVMemory(
    redis,
    on_set=lambda agent, session, key, value: print("SET", agent, session, key),
    on_get=lambda agent, session, key, value: print("GET", agent, session, key),
)

on_get and on_set are optional observability hooks. on_get fires only for values that exist.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
agent, session = "planner-agent", "session-99"

# set / get (a TTL applies to the whole session hash)
kv.set(agent, session, "user_prefs", {"language": "en", "theme": "dark"}, ttl_seconds=600)
kv.set(agent, session, "task_state", {"current_step": 2, "total_steps": 5})
kv.get(agent, session, "user_prefs")          # {"language": "en", "theme": "dark"}
kv.get(agent, session, "missing")             # None

# discoverability
kv.exists(agent, session, "task_state")       # True
kv.keys(agent, session)                       # ["user_prefs", "task_state"]

# bulk
kv.set_many(agent, session, {"scratch": {"notes": []}, "tool_calls": {"count": 0}})
kv.get_many(agent, session, ["user_prefs", "ghost"])   # {"user_prefs": {...}, "ghost": None}

# atomic initialise-once
state = kv.get_or_set(agent, session, "init_flag", lambda: {"initialized": True})

# snapshot / restore
snapshot = kv.dump(agent, session)            # {key: value, ...}
kv.clear(agent, session)                      # delete the whole session
kv.restore(agent, session, snapshot, ttl_seconds=300)

# delete one key
kv.delete(agent, session, "scratch")

docs.title: Through AgentMemory
docs.text:
mem.set_context("status", {"ready": True}, agent_id=agent, session_id=session, ttl_seconds=600)
mem.get_context("status", agent_id=agent, session_id=session)

mem.recall("step", agent_id=agent, session_id=session)["context"]
# context entries whose key or value contains "step" (case-insensitive)

docs.title: Semantics
docs.text:
• TTL — ttl_seconds sets the expiry of the whole session hash (Redis EXPIRE). A later set without a TTL keeps the existing expiry.
  • get_or_set — if the key exists, its value is returned. Otherwise the factory is called and the value is written with HSETNX. If another writer wins the race, their value is returned instead.
  • restore — the same as set_many; it does not clear existing keys first.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Method Description get(agent_id, session_id, key) Value or None set(agent_id, session_id, key, data, *, ttl_seconds=None) Write a value delete(agent_id, session_id, key) Remove one key clear(agent_id, session_id) Delete the whole session hash exists(agent_id, session_id, key) True if present keys(agent_id, session_id) All keys in the session get_many(agent_id, session_id, keys) Dict of key → value (or None) in one round-trip set_many(agent_id, session_id, mapping, *, ttl_seconds=None) Write several keys in one call dump(agent_id, session_id) Export the session as a dict restore(agent_id, session_id, snapshot, *, ttl_seconds=None) Bulk-write a snapshot get_or_set(agent_id, session_id, key, default_factory, *, ttl_seconds=None) Atomic initialise-once

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
This page covers:

  • the databases for Agentic Memory (PostgreSQL, Weaviate, ArangoDB, Redis) on Kubernetes;
  • running the Learner and Incorporator services;
  • running the test suites.

Download Image

docs.title: Databases on Kubernetes
docs.text:
The manifests in agent-memories/k8s/ run all four databases in the agentic-memory namespace and expose them through NodePort services:

Database Manifest Image Workload Container port NodePort Persistent volume PostgreSQL postgres.yaml postgres:16 StatefulSet 5432 30432 postgres-pvc (10 Gi) ArangoDB arango.yaml arangodb:3.12 StatefulSet 8529 30529 arango-pvc (10 Gi) Weaviate weaviate.yaml semitechnologies/weaviate:1.25.0 StatefulSet 8080 (HTTP), 50051 (gRPC) 30880, 30851 weaviate-pvc (10 Gi) Redis redis.yaml redis:7 Deployment 6379 30637 none (data is not persisted)

Weaviate runs with anonymous access and no vectorizer module: Agentic Memory supplies its own embeddings. PostgreSQL, ArangoDB and Redis read their passwords from the postgres-secret, arango-secret and redis-secret Secrets defined in the manifests.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the host directories used by the hostPath volumes (on the node):

    bash mkdir -p /data/agentic-memory/{postgres,arango,weaviate}

  2. Change the passwords in the Secrets in postgres.yaml, arango.yaml and redis.yaml.

  3. Apply the manifests. Volumes go first, so the StatefulSets can bind their claims:

    bash kubectl create namespace agentic-memory # the manifests don't create the namespace kubectl apply -f k8s/pv-pvc.yaml kubectl apply -f k8s/postgres.yaml kubectl apply -f k8s/arango.yaml kubectl apply -f k8s/weaviate.yaml kubectl apply -f k8s/redis.yaml kubectl get pods -n agentic-memory -w

  4. Point Agentic Memory at the node:

    ```python from agentic_memory import MemoryConfig, PostgresConfig, WeaviateConfig, ArangoConfig, RedisConfig

    NODE = "" config = MemoryConfig( postgres=PostgresConfig(host=NODE, port=30432, password=""), weaviate=WeaviateConfig(host=NODE, port=30880, grpc_port=30851), arango=ArangoConfig(url=f"http://{NODE}:30529", password=""), redis=RedisConfig(host=NODE, port=30637, password=""), ) ```

    The examples in agent-memories/examples/ read the same settings from environment variables: POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, ARANGO_URL, ARANGO_PASSWORD, WEAVIATE_HOST, WEAVIATE_PORT, WEAVIATE_GRPC_PORT, REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT and REDIS_PASSWORD.

    The PostgreSQL schema, Weaviate collections and ArangoDB collections are created automatically by the library on first connection.

    The hostPath volumes suit single-node development clusters (minikube, kind, k3s). For production, use a StorageClass/CSI driver instead and do not expose the databases on public NodePorts.

docs.title: Learner and Incorporator Services
docs.text:
Both are FastAPI apps. For a single machine, run them side by side with shared local storage:

export MG_TIDB_DSN="sqlite+aiosqlite:////srv/memorygrid/frame.db"
export MG_LESSONS_ROOT="/srv/memorygrid/lessons_repo"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="..."              # optional; FakeLLMClient is used without it
export MG_LLM_MODEL="claude-sonnet-5-5"

(cd agent-memories/Learner && uvicorn memorygrid_learner.main:app --port 8000) &
(cd agent-memories/Incorporator && \
   MG_FEEDBACK_TIDB_DSN="sqlite+aiosqlite:////srv/memorygrid/feedback.db" \
   MG_DSL_MATCH_RULES_PATH="/srv/memorygrid/dsl_match_rules.json" \
   uvicorn memorygrid_incorporator.main:app --port 8001) &

For multiple machines or production, share real infrastructure:

Setting Learner Incorporator MG_TIDB_DSN TiDB/MySQL (mysql+aiomysql://…) same MG_VECTOR_BACKEND / MG_VECTOR_DSN pgvector or milvus same MG_LESSONS_ROOT Shared volume same MG_FEEDBACK_TIDB_DSN — Feedback DB

TiDB access needs a MySQL async driver (for example aiomysql), which is not in the requirements files. pgvector needs psycopg[binary] and pgvector; Milvus needs pymilvus.

Run one Learner instance, because the scheduler and watcher are in-process. Only the Learner runs the mining schedule and the draft watcher; the Incorporator does not.

docs.title: Running the Tests
docs.text: Package Command Needs services Agentic Memory cd agentic-memory && pytest No (backends are mocked) Agent FS cd fs && pytest No (needs git) Learner cd Learner && pytest -q No (SQLite, in-memory vectors, fake LLM) Incorporator cd Incorporator && pytest -q No (same, plus the sibling Learner/)

docs.title: End-to-End Example
docs.text:
This walkthrough connects every part of Advanced Agent Memories into one loop, using an agent that uploads files to a flaky storage API:

  1. The agent remembers what happens (Agentic Memory).
  2. The Learner mines a lesson from that experience; a human approves it.
  3. At the next task, the Incorporator applies the lesson.
  4. Outcomes are reported; a lesson that keeps failing is escalated.

It assumes the databases are deployed (Deployment) and both services run on one machine with shared storage:

  • Learner on http://localhost:8000
  • Incorporator on http://localhost:8001

docs.title: 1. Record experience
docs.text:
from agentic_memory import AgentMemory
from agentic_memory.models import Outcome

mem = AgentMemory(config)

for attempt in range(3):
    mem.remember_episode("Upload failed with 503, retried with exponential backoff, succeeded",
                         session_id=f"s{attempt}", agent_id="uploader",
                         outcome=Outcome.SUCCESS, importance=0.7,
                         metadata={"action": "retry_with_backoff"})

mem.reflect("Immediate retries make 503s worse",
            lesson="Back off exponentially before retrying uploads")
mem.record_reward("storage API returns 503", "retry_with_backoff", reward=1.0, policy="uploads")
mem.record_reward("storage API returns 503", "retry_immediately", reward=-0.5, policy="uploads")

The agent can already use this directly:

mem.reward.get_best_action("storage is returning 503 errors", policy="uploads")
# ("retry_with_backoff", 1.0)

docs.title: Option A — mine it
docs.text:
The Learner's data sources are in-process. Feed them from Agentic Memory inside the Learner process (see Feeding experience into the Learner), then trigger a run:

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/learner/trigger?time_window=daily"

With the default statistical strategy, three successful retry_with_backoff episodes become a successful_strategy pattern. That produces a draft lesson suggested for the Skills bin. The watcher picks the draft up, enriches it, and it appears in the review queue:

curl http://localhost:8000/lessons/review/queue

docs.title: Option B — an agent suggests it
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/lessons/inject/ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "title": "Retry flaky uploads with backoff",
  "body_md": "When the storage API returns 503, retry uploads with exponential backoff (max 3 tries).",
  "injector_type": "ai_agent",
  "injected_by": "uploader",
  "dsl_payload": {"action": "retry_with_backoff", "instruction_template": "Retry {operation} with backoff"},
  "metadata": {"priority": "high", "criticality": 0.8, "suggested_bin": "skills_base"}
}'

The response has "status": "pending_review" and the lesson id.

docs.title: 3. Human review
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/lessons/review/<lesson_id>/decide \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"decision": "approve"}'

The lesson is now promoted:

  • its file is in lessons_repo/skills/<id>.md and committed to git;
  • it is stored as a skill object and indexed in the vector store.

A human-authored lesson ("injector_type": "human") skips this step and is promoted immediately.

docs.title: 4. Apply the lesson at the next task
docs.text:
Add a DSL rule so flaky_upload problems match the Skills bin deterministically (MG_DSL_MATCH_RULES_PATH):

{"rules": [{"problem_type": "flaky_upload", "target_bin": "skills_base", "query": "retry uploads"}]}

Then, in the agent's pipeline:

from memorygrid_incorporator.pipeline.incorporator_hook import IncorporatorHookClient

hook = IncorporatorHookClient("http://localhost:8001")

outcome = await hook.invoke(
    session_id="s42", problem_solving_step_ref="upload-report",
    problem_type="flaky_upload",
    current_task_context={"operation": "upload report.pdf"},
    system_state={"storage_status": "degraded"},
)
print(outcome.source, outcome.action, outcome.instruction)
# dsl retry_with_backoff Retry upload report.pdf with backoff

docs.title: 5. Report the outcome and close the loop
docs.text:
succeeded = run_upload_with_backoff("report.pdf")       # your executor
await hook.report_outcome("upload-report", "s42", succeeded=succeeded)

mem.remember_episode("Uploaded report.pdf using the backoff lesson",
                     session_id="s42", agent_id="uploader",
                     outcome=Outcome.SUCCESS if succeeded else Outcome.FAILURE,
                     metadata={"action": outcome.action, "lesson_id": outcome.match_result.matched_entity_id})

Watch how the lesson performs:

curl "http://localhost:8001/feedback/metrics/success-rate?lesson_skill_id=<lesson_id>"

If the lesson fails MG_FAILURE_THRESHOLD_X times (3 by default):

  • with MG_REVIEWER_PATH_MODE=human_only, it goes back to pending_review for a human to edit or reject;
  • with auto_only, it is removed from the Skills store immediately;
  • with both, both happen.

New episodes recorded in step 5 feed the next mining run, so the loop keeps improving.

docs.title: 6. Keep agent files under version control (optional)
docs.text:
The agent can keep its working files — plans, generated scripts, reports — in an Agent FS:

from agent_fs import AgentFS

fs = AgentFS("/var/lib/agents", subject_id="uploader")
fs.write("playbooks/uploads.md", "Retry with exponential backoff on 503 (max 3 tries).\n",
         message="adopt backoff lesson")
fs.tag("uploads-playbook-v1", message="after lesson promotion")

docs.title: Episodic Memory
docs.text:
Episodic memory answers "what happened?" An episode is a specific event or experience, tied to a time, a session and an agent: what was asked, what the agent did, and how it turned out.

Use it for session logs, task histories, and any record you later want to search ("have I seen something like this before?"), filter ("what failed today?"), or learn from (reflections and lessons are mined from episodes).

docs.title: Model: EpisodicMemory
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description content str "" What happened (embedded for search) session_id str "" Session the episode belongs to agent_id str "" Agent that experienced it context dict {} Who / when / where / why outcome Outcome UNKNOWN SUCCESS, FAILURE, NEUTRAL or UNKNOWN importance float 0.5 0.0 – 1.0 id, metadata, created_at, score Common fields (see Agentic Memory)

Storage: PostgreSQL (episodic_memories), Weaviate (<prefix>Episodic), ArangoDB (episodic_nodes, linked with memory_relations).

docs.title: Store episodes
docs.text:
from agentic_memory import AgentMemory
from agentic_memory.models import EpisodicMemory, Outcome

with AgentMemory(config) as mem:
    e1 = mem.remember_episode(
        "User asked about the weather forecast for Paris this weekend.",
        session_id="session-42", agent_id="weather-agent",
        context={"user": "alice", "channel": "chat"},
        outcome=Outcome.SUCCESS, importance=0.6,
    )

    # Or build the model yourself
    e2 = EpisodicMemory(content="Weather API timed out", session_id="session-42",
                        agent_id="weather-agent", outcome=Outcome.FAILURE, importance=0.9)
    mem.episodic.store(e2)

docs.title: Search and retrieve
docs.text:
for ep in mem.episodic.search("weather questions about France", top_k=3):
    print(f"{ep.score:.3f}  {ep.outcome.value}  {ep.content}")

ep = mem.episodic.retrieve(e1.id)

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
mem.episodic.get_by_session("session-42")          # oldest first
mem.episodic.get_by_agent("weather-agent", limit=50)   # newest first
mem.episodic.get_by_outcome(Outcome.FAILURE)       # newest first
mem.episodic.get_high_importance(threshold=0.7)    # highest importance first

docs.title: Link episodes (graph)
docs.text:
mem.episodic.link_episodes(e1.id, e2.id, relation="followed_by")
related = mem.episodic.get_related_episodes(e1.id)   # list of episode nodes (dicts)

Links are directed edges in memory_relations. get_related_episodes returns the nodes one hop away in the outbound direction.

Reflections that name an episode as source_episode_id are linked from it automatically; see Reflective Memory.

docs.title: Update and delete
docs.text:
e1.importance = 0.9
e1.outcome = Outcome.SUCCESS
mem.episodic.update(e1)      # re-embeds content and updates all three backends

mem.episodic.delete(e2.id)

update writes content, context, outcome, importance and metadata. session_id and agent_id are not changed by update.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Method Description store(memory) -> str Store an episode retrieve(memory_id) -> EpisodicMemory \| None Load by ID search(query, top_k=5) -> list[EpisodicMemory] Vector similarity search update(memory) Re-embed and overwrite delete(memory_id) Remove from all backends get_by_session(session_id) Episodes in a session, ordered by created_at ascending get_by_agent(agent_id, limit=50) Latest episodes of an agent get_by_outcome(outcome) Episodes with an outcome, newest first get_high_importance(threshold=0.7) Episodes with importance >= threshold link_episodes(from_id, to_id, relation="related") Add a directed graph edge get_related_episodes(memory_id) Episodes linked from this one

docs.title: Incorporator & Feedback
docs.text:
The Incorporator (memorygrid_incorporator, MemoryGrid "Process 3") is how agents use what the Learner has learned. At a step of the agent's problem-solving pipeline it:

  1. matches the current problem against the promoted lessons in the Skills store and the Knowledge Base;
  2. applies the match, turning it into a concrete action for the pipeline to execute;
  3. records feedback for that selection;

and, once the pipeline reports the outcome:

  1. updates feedback and, if a lesson keeps failing, escalates it — back to human review and/or disabling it.

Download Image

The Incorporator imports the Learner package and reuses its storage, LLM client and review queue. Both services must point at the same Skills/Knowledge Base storage (see Sharing storage with the Learner).

docs.title: Running the Service
docs.text:
Requires Python ≥ 3.10 and the Learner/ folder next to Incorporator/. The Learner package is found automatically through the sibling folder, an editable install, or PYTHONPATH.

cd agent-memories/Incorporator
uv venv --python 3.11 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt        # also installs ../Learner/requirements.txt
uvicorn memorygrid_incorporator.main:app --port 8001

docs.title: Configuration (environment variables)
docs.text:
All the Learner variables apply too (MG_TIDB_DSN, MG_VECTOR_BACKEND, MG_VECTOR_DSN, MG_LESSONS_ROOT, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MG_LLM_MODEL, …). The Incorporator adds:

Variable Default Description MG_FEEDBACK_TIDB_DSN sqlite+aiosqlite:///./memorygrid_feedback.db Feedback DB (separate from the lesson store) MG_MATCH_STRATEGY_MODE dsl_then_llm_fallback dsl_only, llm_only, dsl_then_llm_fallback, llm_then_dsl_fallback, best_of_both MG_DSL_MATCH_RULES_PATH ./config/dsl_match_rules.json DSL matcher rules MG_FAILURE_THRESHOLD_X 3 Failures of one lesson that trigger escalation MG_REVIEWER_PATH_MODE human_only human_only, auto_only or both MG_HIL_MODE learner_in_process Human path target: learner_in_process or http MG_HIL_BASE_URL http://localhost:8000 External HIL service (when MG_HIL_MODE=http) MG_AUTO_REMEDIATION_MODE disable_via_learner Auto path target: disable_via_learner or http MG_WORKFLOW_ENGINE_BASE_URL http://localhost:9000 External workflow engine (when MG_AUTO_REMEDIATION_MODE=http)

docs.title: Invoke — POST /incorporator/invoke
docs.text:
Called by the host pipeline at its "Incorporator hook" step:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8001/incorporator/invoke -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "session_id": "s1",
  "problem_solving_step_ref": "step-17",
  "problem_type": "flaky_upload",
  "current_task_context": {"operation": "upload report.pdf"},
  "system_state": {"storage_status": "degraded"},
  "additional_caller_data": {}
}'

QueryInput:

Field Required Description session_id Yes Pipeline session problem_solving_step_ref Yes ID of the pipeline step (used again when reporting the outcome) problem_type Yes Problem category; the key the DSL matcher's rules use current_task_context No Task details (also used to fill instruction templates) system_state No Environment state (given to the LLM applier) additional_caller_data No Anything else (also used to fill instruction templates)

Response — ApplierOutcome:

{
  "id": "6f1c…",
  "source": "dsl",
  "action": "retry_with_backoff",
  "instruction": "Retry upload report.pdf with backoff",
  "recommended_action_payload": {"dsl_payload": {"action": "retry_with_backoff", "instruction_template": "Retry {operation} with backoff"}},
  "match_result": {
    "matched_entity_type": "skill",
    "matched_entity_id": "2b9e…",
    "matcher_used": "dsl",
    "confidence": 1.0,
    "raw_payload": { "...": "the promoted lesson" }
  },
  "created_at": "2026-10-22T10:00:00Z"
}

The pipeline executes action / instruction. If nothing matches, the response is 404.

docs.title: Report outcome — POST /incorporator/outcome
docs.text:
Called after the pipeline evaluates the result:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8001/incorporator/outcome -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"problem_solving_step_ref": "step-17", "session_id": "s1", "result_flag": "failure"}'

result_flag is success, failure or pending. The latest feedback entry for that step and session is updated and returned. The response is 404 if /incorporator/invoke was never called for that step and session.

docs.title: Matching
docs.text:
The Matching Engine combines two matchers according to MG_MATCH_STRATEGY_MODE:

Mode Behaviour dsl_only DSL matcher only llm_only LLM matcher only dsl_then_llm_fallback (default) DSL first; LLM if DSL finds nothing llm_then_dsl_fallback LLM first; DSL if LLM finds nothing best_of_both Run both, keep the higher-confidence match

docs.title: DSL matcher (deterministic, no LLM)
docs.text:
Rules map a problem_type to a bin and a lookup query. They are loaded from MG_DSL_MATCH_RULES_PATH, and no rules apply if the file is missing.

{
  "rules": [
    {"problem_type": "flaky_upload", "target_bin": "skills_base", "query": "retry uploads", "min_score": 0.0},
    {"problem_type": "pricing_question", "target_bin": "knowledge_base", "query": "pricing tiers", "min_score": 0.3}
  ]
}

For the rule of the query's problem_type, the matcher searches that bin with query (or the problem type when no query is set) and takes the top hit. Search combines text match on title/body (score 1.0) with vector similarity. A hit scoring below min_score is ignored.

docs.title: LLM matcher
docs.text:
1. Builds a text query from problem_type, current_task_context and additional_caller_data.
  2. Gets the 10 most similar promoted lessons from the vector store (both bins).
  3. Asks the LLM to choose one ({"lesson_id": ..., "confidence": ...}). If the reply can't be parsed, or the LLM returns no choice, the top vector hit is used.

docs.title: Applying
docs.text:
The Applier chooses between two paths for the matched lesson:

Path When Result DSL picker The lesson's dsl_payload has an action source: "dsl". action is taken from dsl_payload.action. instruction is dsl_payload.instruction_template formatted with current_task_context + additional_caller_data; the raw template is used if a placeholder is missing LLM applier Otherwise source: "llm". The LLM gets the lesson, task context, system state and extra data, and returns {"action", "instruction"}. If the reply can't be parsed, action is apply_recommended_lesson and instruction is the lesson title

To make a lesson deterministic, give it a dsl_payload when you inject it into the Learner:

"dsl_payload": {"action": "retry_with_backoff", "instruction_template": "Retry {operation} with backoff"}

docs.title: Feedback entries
docs.text:
Each successful invoke creates a FeedbackDBEntry in the Feedback DB:

Field Description id Entry ID problem_solving_step_ref, session_id Pipeline step and session lesson_skill_id, matched_entity_type The matched lesson selection_query, selection_context The query and task context result_flag pending → success / failure usage_count 1 at selection, +1 per reported outcome transaction_log_ref ID of the ApplierOutcome timestamp, updated_at

docs.title: Threshold escalation
docs.text:
When a reported outcome is a failure, the Threshold Monitor counts that lesson's failed feedback entries. When the count reaches MG_FAILURE_THRESHOLD_X, the Reviewer Process escalates according to MG_REVIEWER_PATH_MODE:

Path learner_in_process / disable_via_learner (default) http Human path (human_only, both) The original lesson is set back to pending_review, logged with runtime_failure_flagged, and re-queued in the Learner's review queue. A human then approves, edits or rejects it with the Learner review API POST <MG_HIL_BASE_URL>/hil/flagged-lessons with {"lesson_skill_id", "feedback_entry_id", "reason"} Auto path (auto_only, both) The lesson is disabled immediately: deleted from the Skills store and the Knowledge Base (and the vector index), so it can no longer match POST <MG_WORKFLOW_ENGINE_BASE_URL>/events with {"event_type": "lesson_remediation", "payload": {"lesson_skill_id", "failure_count"}}

The http targets are external services you provide. The Learner does not implement /hil/flagged-lessons. Escalation runs again on every further failure once the threshold has been reached.

docs.title: Feedback APIs
Host Pipeline Integration
docs.text:
The package includes a reference client for host pipelines, IncorporatorHookClient:

from memorygrid_incorporator.pipeline.incorporator_hook import IncorporatorHookClient

hook = IncorporatorHookClient("http://localhost:8001")

async def run_step(session_id, step_id, task):
    outcome = await hook.invoke(
        session_id=session_id,
        problem_solving_step_ref=step_id,
        current_task_context={"operation": task.name},
        system_state={"storage_status": "degraded"},
        problem_type=task.problem_type,
    )
    succeeded = await execute(outcome.action, outcome.instruction)   # your executor
    await hook.report_outcome(step_id, session_id, succeeded=succeeded)

invoke raises httpx.HTTPStatusError on a 404 (no match). Fall back to the agent's normal behaviour in that case.

docs.title: Sharing Storage with the Learner
docs.text:
The Incorporator builds its own copies of the Learner's storage objects from the same settings. For it to see the lessons the Learner promotes, both services must share:

  • the object store — the same MG_TIDB_DSN (TiDB/MySQL, or the same SQLite file on one machine);
  • the vector store — MG_VECTOR_BACKEND=pgvector or milvus with the same MG_VECTOR_DSN. The default memory backend is private to each process, so the LLM matcher wouldn't see the other service's lessons;
  • the lessons folder — the same MG_LESSONS_ROOT.

With the default learner_in_process human path, a flagged lesson is re-queued in the Incorporator's in-process copy of the review queue. The flagged lesson's pending_review status is still stored in the shared object store, so it appears in the Learner's GET /lessons/review/queue.

docs.title: Programmatic Use
docs.text:
from memorygrid_incorporator.api.deps import build_dependencies
from memorygrid_incorporator.config import Settings
from memorygrid_incorporator.incorporator.models import QueryInput
from memorygrid_incorporator.feedback.models import ResultFlag

deps = build_dependencies(Settings())

query = QueryInput(session_id="s1", problem_solving_step_ref="step-1", problem_type="flaky_upload",
                   current_task_context={"operation": "upload"})
match = await deps.matching_engine.match(query)
outcome = await deps.applier_service.apply(match, query)
await deps.feedback_recorder.record_selection(query, match, outcome)

entry = await deps.feedback_updater.update("step-1", "s1", ResultFlag.FAILURE)
await deps.threshold_monitor.check_and_escalate(entry)

deps.learner_deps is the Learner's full dependency container (stores, review service, …).

docs.title: Learner
docs.text:
The Learner (memorygrid_learner, MemoryGrid "Process 2") turns experience into lessons that agents can trust. A lesson reaches agents in one of three ways:

  • it is mined, on a schedule or on demand, from episodic logs, task outcomes and other memory sources;
  • it is injected by a human or by another agent;
  • it is requested from a peer agent's Skills store or Knowledge Base (cross-agent sharing, read-only).

Mined and agent-injected lessons are enriched (why the lesson matters, evidence, priority, a suggested bin) and go to human review. Approved lessons are promoted to one of two bins:

Bin BinType Holds Skills skills_base Procedural knowledge, how-to patterns Knowledge Base knowledge_base Semantic facts, domain knowledge

Every lesson is stored as a Markdown file, a database record and a vector embedding, and every change is a git commit.

Download Image

docs.title: Lesson Lifecycle
docs.text:
mined (pipeline)                    injected (ai_agent)              injected (human)
                  │                                    │                              │
                  ▼                                    ▼                              │
               DRAFT ──► watcher ──► enrichment ──► PENDING_REVIEW                    │
                                                       │                              │
                              human decision ◄─────────┘                              │
                     ┌───────────────┼────────────────────┐                           │
                  approve     edit_then_approve         reject                        │
                     │               │                     │                          │
                  APPROVED     EDITED_APPROVED          REJECTED ─► archive/          │
                     └───────┬───────┘                                                │
                             ▼                                                        ▼
                         PROMOTED  ◄──────────────────────────────── (skips review) APPROVED
                   skills/ or kb/  + DB + vector + git commit
Status Meaning draft Created by the pipeline (or just persisted), not yet enriched pending_enrichment Reserved for enrichment in progress pending_review Enriched and waiting for a human decision approved / edited_approved Human approved (with or without edits) rejected Rejected; file moved to archive/ and the reason logged promoted Written to the Skills store or Knowledge Base and committed

Every transition is appended to the lesson's audit_trail.

docs.title: Running the Service
docs.text:
