Use last_executed_batch to see which nodes just ran Router routes to itself WorkflowRouterError The router node cannot appear in its own response Router returns a step with a nodeID not in nodes WorkflowRouterError Every step must reference a defined node Router or agent on_preprocess returns None The workflow hangs — the executor waits for a result that never arrives Always return [task] from the router; return an error AgentResult from agents instead of skipping Not merging initial_input into downstream node inputs Later nodes lose the original request data Always spread initial_input into every step's input dict Typo in nodeID string in router A typo in a comparison silently falls through to the fallback [] and ends the workflow; a typo in a returned step raises WorkflowRouterError Use constants for all node ID strings model_name missing on agent node Warning at runtime, unpredictable agent behaviour Always set model_name in agent settings Sub-workflow id doesn't match a registered workflow_uri WorkflowNodeError on the workflow node at runtime Ensure the target workflow is registered in the workflow service with the exact URI

docs.title: Workflow Onboarding Guide
docs.text: A step-by-step guide to defining, registering, deploying, and executing workflows.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Overview
  2. Step 1 — Author the Workflow Spec (JSON)
  3. Step 2 — Register the Workflow
  4. Step 3 — Deploy the Workflow Controller
  5. Step 4 — Execute a Task
  6. End-to-End Example
  7. Reference — Node Types
  8. Reference — Graph Types
  9. Common Mistakes

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
Onboarding a workflow involves four steps:

1. Author JSON Spec   →   Define nodes + graph in a .json file
2. Register Spec      →   POST the JSON to /api/workflows (workflow service)
3. Deploy Controller  →   POST to /api/deploy-workflow/<deployer_id> to spin up a workflow executor
4. Execute Task       →   POST to <executor url>/api/execute with your input payload

Each step is described in detail below.

docs.title: 2. Step 1 — Author the Workflow Spec (JSON)
docs.text: A workflow spec is a JSON document with two top-level sections: header and body.

docs.title: 2.1 Header
docs.text:
The header identifies the workflow and generates its workflow_uri in the format:

{name}:{version}-{release}

"header": {
  "workflow_id": {
    "name":    "my-workflow",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "release": "stable"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "description": "What this workflow does",
    "owner":       "your-team",
    "created_at":  "2026-03-01"
  }
}
Field Rules name Lowercase kebab-case. E.g. loan-approval, fraud-detection version Semantic versioning. E.g. 1.0.0, 2.1.0 release Maturity tag. Use stable, beta, or rc1

Note: Do not set workflow_uri manually — it is computed by the workflow service when the spec is registered.

docs.title: 2.2 Nodes
docs.text:
Each node in body.nodes is one step in the pipeline.

Agent Node — runs an AI agent:

{
  "nodeID": "my-agent",
  "type": "agent",
  "id": "agents/my-agent-subject-id",
  "settings": {
    "model_name": "aios:qwen3-1-7b-vllm-block"
  }
}

Policy Node — runs deterministic rules or logic:

{
  "nodeID": "validate-input",
  "type": "policy",
  "id": "rules/validate-v1",
  "policyType": "local",
  "settings": {},
  "parameters": { "strict_mode": true }
}

Workflow Node — delegates to another registered workflow:

{
  "nodeID": "fraud-investigation-workflow",
  "type": "workflow",
  "id": "fraud-investigation:1.0.0-stable"
}

docs.title: 2.3 Graph
docs.text:
The graph defines how nodes connect. Two types are supported.

Static Graph — fixed execution order defined upfront ("type": "static" is optional):

"graph": {
  "node-a": ["node-b", "node-c"],
  "node-b": ["node-d"],
  "node-c": ["node-d"]
}

Dynamic Graph — a router agent decides execution order at runtime:

"graph": {
  "type": "dynamic",
  "nodeID": "router-agent"
}

docs.title: 2.4 Complete Spec Example
docs.text:
Below is the complete spec for a Legal Contract Review Pipeline — a linear static workflow with five agents:

{
  "header": {
    "workflow_id": {
      "name": "legal-contract-review-pipeline-1",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "release": "stable"
    },
    "metadata": {
      "description": "Multi-agent pipeline to review contracts, flag risks and produce a legal memo",
      "owner": "legal-ops-team",
      "created_at": "2026-03-09"
    }
  },
  "body": {
    "nodes": [
      {
        "nodeID": "clause-extractor-agent",
        "type": "agent",
        "id": "w1-clause-1",
        "settings": { "model_name": "aios:qwen3-1-7b-vllm-block" }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "risk-identifier-agent",
        "type": "agent",
        "id": "w1-risk-1",
        "settings": { "model_name": "aios:qwen3-1-7b-vllm-block" }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "compliance-checker-agent",
        "type": "agent",
        "id": "w1-comp-1",
        "settings": { "model_name": "aios:qwen3-1-7b-vllm-block" }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "negotiation-advisor-agent",
        "type": "agent",
        "id": "w1-nego-1",
        "settings": { "model_name": "aios:qwen3-1-7b-vllm-block" }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "legal-memo-agent",
        "type": "agent",
        "id": "w1-memo-1",
        "settings": { "model_name": "aios:qwen3-1-7b-vllm-block" }
      }
    ],
    "graph": {
      "clause-extractor-agent":    ["risk-identifier-agent"],
      "risk-identifier-agent":     ["compliance-checker-agent"],
      "compliance-checker-agent":  ["negotiation-advisor-agent"],
      "negotiation-advisor-agent": ["legal-memo-agent"]
    }
  }
}

This produces the following pipeline:

clause-extractor-agent
        ↓
risk-identifier-agent
        ↓
compliance-checker-agent
        ↓
negotiation-advisor-agent
        ↓
legal-memo-agent

docs.title: 3. Step 2 — Register the Workflow
docs.text:
Once your spec JSON is ready, register it with the workflow service.

Request:

curl -X POST \
  -d @./spec.json \
  http://<HOST>:<PORT>/api/workflows

What this does: Stores the workflow spec in the workflow service's database (MongoDB). The service parses the header and stores the spec under the computed workflow_uri (e.g. legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable).

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "header": {
      "workflow_id":  { "name": "...", "version": "...", "release": "..." },
      "workflow_uri": "legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable",
      "metadata":     { "description": "...", "owner": "...", "created_at": "..." }
    },
    "body": { "nodes": [ ... ], "graph": { ... } }
  }
}

Notes:

  • Registration does not validate the spec. Errors such as duplicate nodeIDs or graph references to undefined nodes are only detected when the workflow executor loads the spec (Step 3).
  • Only the known fields are stored. Unknown keys on nodes or in metadata are dropped.
  • Registering a workflow_uri that already exists fails with HTTP 400 (Workflow <uri> already exists). To change an existing workflow, use PUT /api/workflows/<workflow_uri> (see Managing Registered Workflows).

Tip: Save your spec as spec.json in your working directory before running the command.

docs.title: Managing Registered Workflows
docs.text:
All endpoints are on the workflow service and return { "success": ..., "data": ... } (or "message" on error).

Method & Path Description GET /api/workflows/<workflow_uri> Get a workflow spec (404 if not found) PUT /api/workflows/<workflow_uri> Replace a workflow spec (body: full spec JSON). The stored workflow_uri is kept PATCH /api/workflows/<workflow_uri> Update fields: body { "update": { "<dotted.field>": <value> } } (MongoDB $set) DELETE /api/workflows/<workflow_uri> Delete a workflow spec GET /api/workflows?limit=50&skip=0 List workflows POST /api/workflows/query Query workflows: body { "query": {...}, "projection": {...}, "sort": [...], "limit": 50, "skip": 0 }

docs.title: 4. Step 3 — Deploy the Workflow Controller
docs.text:
After registration, deploy a workflow executor that will run the workflow. The workflow service forwards the request to the agent deployer identified by DEPLOYER_ID, which creates a Kubernetes Deployment (one replica) and a NodePort Service named <deployment_name>-svc in the workflows namespace. The executor listens on port 9100.

Request:

curl -X POST \
  http://<HOST>:<PORT>/api/deploy-workflow/<DEPLOYER_ID> \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "deployment_name": "<your-deployment-name>",
    "workflow_id":     "<unique-instance-id>",
    "workflow_uri":    "<name>:<version>-<release>",
    "allocation": {
      "policy_db_url":    "http://<POLICY_HOST>:<PORT>",
      "delegate_api_url": "http://<AGENT_HOST>:<PORT>"
    }
  }'

Fields:

Field Required Description DEPLOYER_ID Yes ID of a registered agent deployer (path param). 404 if not found deployment_name Yes Name of the Kubernetes Deployment. It is lower-cased, characters other than a-z, 0-9 and - are replaced with -, and it is truncated to 63 characters. Deploying again with the same name replaces the existing Deployment workflow_id Yes Unique ID of this runtime workflow record. Must not already exist workflow_uri Yes Must match the workflow_uri of the registered spec exactly cluster_id No Cluster identifier stored on the runtime record allocation.policy_db_url Yes Base URL of the Policy DB, used by local policy nodes allocation.delegate_api_url Yes Base URL of the agent Delegate API

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "id":              "simple-workflow-001",
    "workflow_uri":    "legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable",
    "cluster_id":      null,
    "deployer_id":     "deployer-111",
    "deployment_name": "simple-workflow",
    "url":             "http://<deployer_ip>:<node_port>"
  }
}

data.url is the base URL of the deployed workflow executor — use it in Step 4. The record is stored as a runtime workflow and can be read later:

Method & Path Description GET /api/runtime-workflows/<workflow_id> Get a runtime workflow GET /api/runtime-workflows?workflow_uri=<uri>&cluster_id=<id>&limit=50&skip=0 List runtime workflows (filters optional) DELETE /api/runtime-workflows/<workflow_id> Delete the runtime record only (does not remove the Kubernetes resources)

Example:

curl -X POST \
  http://35.223.239.192:30721/api/deploy-workflow/deployer-111 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "deployment_name": "simple-workflow",
    "workflow_id":     "simple-workflow-001",
    "workflow_uri":    "legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable",
    "allocation": {
      "policy_db_url":    "http://34.58.1.86:30102",
      "delegate_api_url": "http://35.223.239.192:30725"
    }
  }'

Note: The workflow_uri in the deploy request must exactly match the registered spec — including name, version, and release. The deploy request itself still succeeds on a mismatch. The error appears when the executor starts: it cannot fetch the spec (WorkflowDBError), fails to start, and Kubernetes keeps restarting it. An invalid spec (WorkflowSpecError, WorkflowCycleError) has the same effect. Check the executor pod logs in the workflows namespace if /api/execute is unreachable.

Known issue: The deployer passes delegate_api_url to the executor as the DELEGATE_API_URL environment variable, but the executor reads DELGATE_API_URL. Until this is fixed, agent nodes use the executor's built-in default Delegate API URL rather than the value in allocation.

docs.title: Removing a Deployed Workflow
docs.text:
curl -X POST \
  http://<HOST>:<PORT>/api/remove-workflow/<DEPLOYER_ID>/<workflow_id>

This deletes the executor's Deployment and Service and the runtime workflow record. The registered spec is kept.

docs.title: 5. Step 4 — Execute a Task
docs.text:
With the executor deployed, submit a task to the executor URL returned by the deploy step (data.url).

Request:

curl -X POST \
  <EXECUTOR_URL>/api/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "text": "<your input payload>"
  }'

The body must be a JSON object; it becomes the workflow's initial_input.

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "<nodeID>": { "...": "output of that node" },
    "<nodeID>": { "...": "..." }
  }
}

data maps each executed nodeID to its output. For a dynamic workflow whose router returned a final-output dict, data is that dict instead.

Errors return { "success": false, "error": "<message>" }:

HTTP status Cause 400 WorkflowSpecError — e.g. the body is not a JSON object 500 WorkflowNodeError (response also includes node_id), WorkflowRouterError, WorkflowExecutionError, WorkflowDBError, or any other error

The request is synchronous — it returns only when the whole workflow has finished. The executor also exposes GET /health.

Example (here http://35.223.239.192:30712 is the data.url returned by the deploy step):

curl -X POST \
  http://35.223.239.192:30712/api/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "text": "Contract: SaaS Subscription Agreement between Acme Corp (vendor) and RetailCo (client). Key clauses: auto-renewal at 15% price increase, no SLA guarantees, data ownership ambiguous, termination requires 180-day notice, liability cap at $5,000 regardless of contract value ($2M/year). Jurisdiction: Delaware, USA."
  }'

The input is passed as initial_input to the entry node(s) of the pipeline. Each subsequent node receives the output of its parent node(s).

docs.title: 6. End-to-End Example
docs.text: Here is the complete flow for the Legal Contract Review Pipeline:

docs.title: Step 1 — Save the spec
docs.text:
# Save the JSON spec from Section 2.4 as spec.json
vim spec.json

docs.title: Step 2 — Register
docs.text:
curl -X POST \
  -d @./spec.json \
  http://35.223.239.192:30721/api/workflows

docs.title: Step 3 — Deploy
docs.text:
curl -X POST \
  http://35.223.239.192:30721/api/deploy-workflow/deployer-111 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "deployment_name": "legal-contract-review",
    "workflow_id":     "legal-review-001",
    "workflow_uri":    "legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable",
    "allocation": {
      "policy_db_url":    "http://34.58.1.86:30102",
      "delegate_api_url": "http://35.223.239.192:30725"
    }
  }'

docs.title: Step 4 — Execute
docs.text:
Use the data.url returned by Step 3 as the executor URL:

curl -X POST \
  http://35.223.239.192:30712/api/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "text": "Contract: SaaS Subscription Agreement between Acme Corp (vendor) and RetailCo (client)..."
  }'

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
Input text
    ↓
clause-extractor-agent     → extracts all clauses from the contract
    ↓
risk-identifier-agent      → identifies risky clauses
    ↓
compliance-checker-agent   → checks against legal standards
    ↓
negotiation-advisor-agent  → recommends negotiation points
    ↓
legal-memo-agent           → produces the final legal memo

docs.title: 7. Reference — Node Types
docs.text: Type Use Case Required Fields agent Run an AI agent nodeID, type, id (settings.model_name strongly recommended) policy Run deterministic rules/logic nodeID, type, id, policyType (+ settings required by the policy type) workflow Delegate to another workflow nodeID, type, id (must be a valid workflow_uri)

docs.title: Policy Types
docs.text: policyType When to Use local Simple rule evaluated in-process central Rule engine hosted on a remote service function Serverless/function endpoint job Long-running batch job that requires polling

docs.title: 8. Reference — Graph Types
docs.text:
Type When to Use Static Execution order is always the same. All branches always run. Dynamic Branches depend on output content. Loops or retries are needed. A router agent decides what runs next.

Rule of thumb: If you would need an if statement to decide the next step — use Dynamic.

docs.title: 9. Common Mistakes
docs.text: Mistake What Goes Wrong Fix workflow_uri in deploy doesn't match registered spec Executor fails at start-up with WorkflowDBError and keeps restarting Copy the URI exactly from the header: {name}:{version}-{release} Reusing a workflow_id in a deploy request Deploy returns 400 (runtime workflow already exists), although the Kubernetes Deployment is created or replaced Use a new workflow_id, or remove the existing deployment first Duplicate nodeID values in nodes WorkflowSpecError when the executor starts (not at registration) Every node must have a unique nodeID Graph references a nodeID not defined in nodes WorkflowSpecError when the executor starts (not at registration) Ensure all IDs in the graph match node definitions exactly policyType missing on a policy node WorkflowSpecError Always set policyType for every policy node model_name missing on an agent node Warning at runtime, unpredictable behaviour Always set model_name in settings Sub-workflow id doesn't match a registered workflow_uri WorkflowNodeError on the workflow node at runtime Ensure the target workflow is registered before referencing it An agent's on_preprocess returns None /api/execute never returns Return an error AgentResult instead of skipping Typo in a nodeID string Silent routing failure Double-check all node IDs — copy-paste rather than retype

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Schema Reference
  2. Guide to Creating Workflows
  3. Complete Workflow JSON Examples

docs.title: 1. Schema Reference
docs.text: A Workflow JSON is a structured object composed of two top-level keys: header and body.

docs.title: 1.1 Top-Level Structure
docs.text: Field Type Required Description header object Yes Identity and metadata for the workflow body object Yes Nodes and graph definition for the workflow

docs.title: 1.2 header
docs.text: Field Type Required Description workflow_id object Yes Unique identity of the workflow metadata object No Descriptive information about the workflow workflow_uri string Auto Computed by the workflow service as name:version-release when the workflow is registered. Do not set manually — any value you provide is overwritten.

docs.title: header.workflow_id
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes Workflow name (e.g., fraud-detection) version string Yes Semantic version (e.g., 1.0) release string Yes Release tag (e.g., stable, beta, rc1)

docs.title: header.metadata
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description description string No Human-readable purpose of the workflow owner string No Team or individual responsible created_at string No ISO 8601 timestamp of creation

The workflow service stores only these three metadata fields; any other keys under metadata are dropped on registration.

docs.title: 1.3 body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description nodes array of objects Yes List of all nodes (steps) in the workflow graph object No Defines execution order. If omitted (or empty), every node is an entry node: nodes run one after another in the order they are declared, and each receives the workflow's initial input.

docs.title: 1.4 Node Fields (body.nodes[])
docs.text:
Each node in the nodes array is an object with the following fields:

Field Type Required Description nodeID string Yes Unique, non-empty identifier for this node within the workflow type string Yes Node type. One of: policy, agent, workflow id string Yes Non-empty reference to the resource — policy rule URI, function ID, agent subject ID, or sub-workflow workflow_uri policyType string Yes (if type=policy) One of: local, central, function, job settings object Conditional Node-level configuration. Required keys depend on policyType parameters object No Runtime arguments passed to the policy executor (used by local, central and job policies)

The workflow service persists only the fields listed above for each node. Any additional keys on a node are dropped when the workflow is registered.

docs.title: settings Required Keys by policyType
docs.text:
policyType Required settings keys Optional settings keys local (none) — central executor_id, endpoint — function endpoint — job executor_id, endpoint job_name, node_selector, poll_interval, max_retries

Note: endpoint must be a string starting with http (e.g. http://… or https://…). poll_interval and max_retries must be positive integers.

Defaults for optional job settings:

Key Default job_name job-<nodeID>-<8 random hex chars> node_selector {} poll_interval 2 (seconds) max_retries 30 (polling attempts)

docs.title: settings for agent nodes
docs.text:
Key Type Required Description model_name string No* Model to run the agent with. Strongly recommended.

*Omitting model_name on an agent node will log a warning but will not fail validation. The value (or an empty string) is always sent to the agent as task_data.model_name.

docs.title: 1.5 body.graph
docs.text: The graph object controls how nodes are connected and in what order they execute. It supports two modes: static and dynamic.

docs.title: Static Graph
docs.text: Field Type Required Description type string No Set to "static" (default if type is omitted). Must be "static" or "dynamic". <nodeID> array of strings No Each key is a parent nodeID; value is a list of child nodeIDs

docs.title: Dynamic Graph
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description type string Yes Must be "dynamic" nodeID string Yes The nodeID of the router node that controls execution at runtime

Any other keys in a dynamic graph are ignored (a warning is logged).

docs.title: 2.1 Node Types
docs.text: There are three types of nodes available in a workflow.

docs.title: 2.1.1 Policy Node (type: "policy")
docs.text:
A policy node runs a deterministic rule or function. It requires a policyType field, which determines which executor is used and what settings are needed.

policyType What it does local Evaluates a policy rule locally using LocalType1Evaluator central Calls a centralized policy executor via a remote endpoint function Invokes a serverless/function endpoint directly job Submits a long-running job to an executor and polls for completion

How each policyType is executed:

policyType Request made by the workflow executor Result used local Fetches the policy (code, parameters, settings) for id from the Policy DB at POLICY_DB_URL, then runs it in-process with the node input. Node parameters are merged with the policy's stored parameters; on a key conflict the stored policy value wins. The policy is fetched and initialised each time the node runs. Return value of the policy central POST {endpoint}/executor/{executor_id}/execute_policy with {"policy_rule_uri": id, "input_data": <input>, "parameters": <parameters>} data field of the response (response must have success: true) function POST {endpoint}/function/call_function/{id} with the node input as the JSON body data field of the response (response must have success: true) job POST {endpoint}/jobs/submit/{executor_id} with {"name": job_name, "policy_rule_uri": id, "policy_rule_parameters": <parameters>, "node_selector": ..., "inputs": <input>}, then polls GET {endpoint}/jobs/{job_id} every poll_interval seconds, up to max_retries times data.job_output_data once data.job_status == "completed"; a TimeoutError (reported as a node failure) otherwise

Remote calls (central, function, job submit/poll) use a 10-second HTTP timeout.

local policy — simplest type, no remote dependencies:

{
  "nodeID": "eligibility-check",
  "type": "policy",
  "id": "rules/eligibility-v1",
  "policyType": "local",
  "settings": {},
  "parameters": { "threshold": 0.8 }
}

central policy — delegates to a central rules engine:

{
  "nodeID": "risk-score",
  "type": "policy",
  "id": "rules/risk-scoring-v2",
  "policyType": "central",
  "settings": {
    "executor_id": "central-executor-01",
    "endpoint": "https://rules-engine.internal/execute"
  },
  "parameters": { "context": "loan-application" }
}

function policy — calls a lightweight function endpoint:

{
  "nodeID": "format-output",
  "type": "policy",
  "id": "functions/formatter",
  "policyType": "function",
  "settings": {
    "endpoint": "https://functions.internal/format"
  }
}

job policy — submits a batch job and waits for results:

{
  "nodeID": "ml-scoring-job",
  "type": "policy",
  "id": "rules/ml-score-v3",
  "policyType": "job",
  "settings": {
    "executor_id": "job-executor-gpu",
    "endpoint": "https://jobs.internal/submit",
    "job_name": "ml-score-run-001",
    "poll_interval": 5,
    "max_retries": 60
  }
}

docs.title: 2.1.2 Agent Node (type: "agent")
docs.text:
An agent node delegates execution to an AI agent via the Delegate API (/api/submit-and-wait). The agent is identified by id (its subject_id) and the model to use is specified in settings.model_name.

{
  "nodeID": "summarize-agent",
  "type": "agent",
  "id": "agents/summarizer-subject",
  "settings": {
    "model_name": "gpt-4o"
  }
}

The executor generates a session_id and task_id (both UUIDs) and posts the following to the Delegate API:

{
  "subject_id": "<node id>",
  "session_id": "<uuid>",
  "task_id":    "<uuid>",
  "task_data":  { "...node input...": "...", "model_name": "<settings.model_name>" }
}
  • The node input becomes the agent's job_data, with model_name added to it.
  • If the node input is not a dict (for example, a list from multiple parents), it is wrapped as {"data": <input>}.
  • The executor returns output.job_output from the Delegate API response. A missing output.job_output is a node failure. is_error in the agent result is not checked — an agent error result is passed downstream as its (usually empty) job_output.
  • The Delegate API URL is read from the DELGATE_API_URL environment variable of the workflow executor, falling back to a built-in default.

docs.title: 2.1.3 Workflow Node (type: "workflow")
docs.text:
A workflow node runs another workflow as a sub-workflow, enabling composition and nesting. The id field is the workflow_uri of the target workflow, which is fetched from the DB at runtime.

{
  "nodeID": "pre-processing-workflow",
  "type": "workflow",
  "id": "data-preprocessing:1.0-stable"
}

The sub-workflow is executed using a fresh AgentDSLWorkflowExecutor instance with this node's input (a non-dict input is wrapped as {"data": <input>}). Its result — the outputs dict, or the terminal output returned by its router if it is dynamic — becomes this node's output. Any failure inside the sub-workflow (including a fetch or spec error) is reported as a WorkflowNodeError on this node.

docs.title: 2.2.1 Static Workflow
docs.text:
In a static workflow the execution order is fully determined at initialization time using a topological sort (Kahn's algorithm). You define an adjacency list where each key is a parent node and its value is the list of nodes it feeds into.

Input resolution rules: - A node with no parents receives the initial_input of the workflow. This includes nodes that do not appear in the graph at all. - A node with one parent receives that parent's output directly. - A node with multiple parents receives a list of all parent outputs. - Nodes run one at a time, in topological order. Entry nodes start in the order they are declared in nodes. - A node that returns None is treated as returning {}. - The workflow result is a dict of nodeID → output for all nodes.

Constraints: - No cycles allowed (will raise WorkflowCycleError). - No self-loops. - All nodeID references in the graph must exist in nodes.

"graph": {
  "type": "static",
  "node-a": ["node-b", "node-c"],
  "node-b": ["node-d"],
  "node-c": ["node-d"]
}

This defines the execution order: node-a → node-b, node-c → node-d.

docs.title: 2.2.2 Dynamic Workflow (Router)
docs.text:
In a dynamic workflow, execution order is not predetermined. Instead, a designated router node is called repeatedly at runtime. The router is called once at the start, and then once after each batch of nodes it returned has finished. The nodes in a batch run one after another, in the order listed.

The router receives a payload containing:

Key Description initial_input The original input passed to execute() history Ordered list of all nodeIDs executed so far outputs Map of nodeID → output for all completed nodes last_executed The last {nodeID, output} dict of the last batch (None on the first call) last_executed_batch List of all {nodeID, output} dicts from the last batch ([] on the first call)

For an agent router, this payload is sent as the agent's task_data (with model_name added).

The router's output (job_output for an agent router) is interpreted as follows:

Router output Result A non-empty list of { "nodeID": "...", "input": {...} } steps The steps run in order, then the router is called again An empty list, None, or {} The workflow is complete; the outputs map is returned A dict with one key next_steps, steps, nodes, data or result holding a list That list is used as the steps A dict with more than one key Treated as the final output: the workflow ends and returns this dict instead of outputs

Each step's input defaults to {}; a non-dict input is wrapped as {"data": <input>}.

"graph": {
  "type": "dynamic",
  "nodeID": "router-agent"
}

The router node itself must be defined in body.nodes. It is typically an agent node whose underlying model decides the next steps. Each step must reference a node defined in body.nodes, and the router cannot route to itself — both raise WorkflowRouterError.

docs.title: 2.3 Validation Rules Summary
docs.text:
Spec validation runs when the workflow executor loads the workflow (at executor start-up). Registering a workflow with the workflow service does not validate it.

Rule Error Raised Missing header or body WorkflowSpecError body.nodes missing or not a list WorkflowSpecError Node missing nodeID, type or id WorkflowSpecError Missing name, version, or release in workflow_id WorkflowSpecError Duplicate nodeID values WorkflowSpecError Unknown node type UnknownNodeTypeError Policy node missing policyType WorkflowSpecError Unknown policyType UnknownPolicyTypeError Missing required settings keys for policy WorkflowSpecError Invalid endpoint (not an HTTP URL) WorkflowSpecError poll_interval / max_retries not a positive int WorkflowSpecError graph.type not static or dynamic WorkflowSpecError Graph references a nodeID not in nodes WorkflowSpecError Static graph value is not a list of strings WorkflowSpecError Cycle detected in static graph WorkflowCycleError Self-loop in static graph WorkflowCycleError Dynamic graph missing nodeID (router) WorkflowSpecError Router node does not exist in nodes WorkflowSpecError

Errors raised while a workflow runs:

Situation Error Raised A node fails (HTTP error, bad response, exception, sub-workflow failure) WorkflowNodeError (carries node_id) Router returns an invalid response, a step without nodeID, an unknown nodeID, or itself WorkflowRouterError Workflow spec cannot be fetched from the workflow service WorkflowDBError

UnknownNodeTypeError and UnknownPolicyTypeError are subclasses of WorkflowSpecError; WorkflowCycleError is not.

docs.text:

  },

        "nodeID": "ingest",

        "id": "rules/normalize-application",
        "policyType": "local",
        "settings": {}
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "risk-check",
        "type": "policy",
        "id": "rules/risk-score-v3",
        "policyType": "central",
        "settings": {
          "executor_id": "risk-executor",
          "endpoint": "https://risk.internal/execute"
        },
        "parameters": { "model": "xgb-v2" }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "compliance-check",
        "type": "policy",
        "id": "rules/aml-compliance",
        "policyType": "function",
        "settings": {
          "endpoint": "https://compliance.internal/check"
        }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "final-decision",
        "type": "agent",
        "id": "agents/loan-decision-subject",
        "settings": {
          "model_name": "gpt-4o"
        }
      }
    ],

      "ingest": ["risk-check", "compliance-check"],
      "risk-check": ["final-decision"],
      "compliance-check": ["final-decision"]
    }

}

final-decision has two parents, so its input is the list [risk-check output, compliance-check output]. Because it is an agent node, the list is wrapped and the agent receives {"data": [risk-check output, compliance-check output], "model_name": "gpt-4o"}. Parent order follows the order of the graph entries.

docs.title: 3.3 Dynamic Workflow with a Router Agent
docs.text:
The router agent decides at runtime which nodes to invoke and in what order.

    }
  },
  "body": {
    "nodes": [
      {
        "nodeID": "router-agent",
        "type": "agent",
        "id": "agents/triage-router-subject",
        "settings": {
          "model_name": "gpt-4o"
        }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "classify-intent",
        "type": "policy",
        "id": "rules/intent-classifier",
        "policyType": "function",
        "settings": {
          "endpoint": "https://nlp.internal/classify"
        }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "fetch-account",
        "type": "policy",
        "id": "rules/account-lookup",
        "policyType": "central",
        "settings": {
          "executor_id": "crm-executor",
          "endpoint": "https://crm.internal/execute"
        }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "generate-response",
        "type": "agent",
        "id": "agents/response-gen-subject",
        "settings": {
          "model_name": "gpt-4o"
        }
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "escalate-to-human",
        "type": "policy",
        "id": "rules/escalation-trigger",
        "policyType": "local",
        "settings": {}
      }
    ],
    "graph": {
      "type": "dynamic",
      "nodeID": "router-agent"
    }
  }
}

At runtime, router-agent receives the full state (history, outputs, last executed batch) and returns a list of next steps. It may choose to run classify-intent first, then decide between generate-response or escalate-to-human based on the result. When it returns an empty list or None, the workflow ends and the outputs map is returned.

docs.text:
Calls a separately deployed workflow as a step within a larger workflow.

    }
  },

    "nodes": [
      {
        "nodeID": "pre-process",
        "type": "workflow",
        "id": "data-preprocessing:1.2-stable"
      },
      {
        "nodeID": "score",
        "type": "policy",
        "id": "rules/ml-scoring-v4",
        "policyType": "job",
        "settings": {
          "executor_id": "gpu-executor-01",
          "endpoint": "https://jobs.internal/submit",
          "poll_interval": 10,
          "max_retries": 30
        }
      },

        "type": "agent",
        "id": "agents/summary-subject",

pre-process is an entry node, so it receives the workflow's initial input. It fetches data-preprocessing:1.2-stable from the workflow service, runs it in a nested executor with that input, and its complete outputs map becomes the input of score.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The Legal Contract Review Pipeline is a five-agent static workflow that takes raw contract text as input and produces a structured legal memo with risk findings, compliance analysis, redline suggestions, and a final recommendation.

What it does, end to end:

Raw contract text
        ↓
  Extract clauses          (clause-extractor-agent)
        ↓
  Identify risks           (risk-identifier-agent)
        ↓
  Check compliance         (compliance-checker-agent)
        ↓
  Advise on redlines       (negotiation-advisor-agent)
        ↓
  Produce legal memo       (legal-memo-agent)

Infrastructure used:

Component Address Used for Workflow Service http://35.223.239.192:30721 Registering and deploying workflows Agent Delegate API http://35.223.239.192:30725 Running agent nodes (/api/submit-and-wait) Policy DB http://34.58.1.86:30102 local policy nodes (not used by this pipeline) Workflow Executor http://35.223.239.192:30712 Executing tasks. This address is the url returned by the deploy step, so yours will differ

docs.title: Execution Flow
docs.text:
The pipeline is static and linear — each agent runs sequentially and passes its full output to the next agent.

┌─────────────────────────┐
│   clause-extractor-agent │  ← receives: { "text": "<contract>" }
└────────────┬────────────┘
             ↓
┌─────────────────────────┐
│   risk-identifier-agent  │  ← receives: clauses{}
└────────────┬────────────┘
             ↓
┌──────────────────────────┐
│  compliance-checker-agent │  ← receives: clauses{} + risks[]
└────────────┬─────────────┘
             ↓
┌───────────────────────────┐
│  negotiation-advisor-agent │  ← receives: risks[] + compliance_findings[]
└────────────┬──────────────┘
             ↓
┌─────────────────────────┐
│     legal-memo-agent     │  ← receives: full accumulated payload
└─────────────────────────┘
             ↓
      Legal Memo Output

docs.title: Accumulated Payload
docs.text:
Each agent carries forward all upstream fields plus its own additions. By the time legal-memo-agent runs, the full payload is:

Field Added By raw_contract clause-extractor-agent clauses clause-extractor-agent clause_count clause-extractor-agent risks risk-identifier-agent overall_risk_score risk-identifier-agent high_risk_count risk-identifier-agent compliance_findings compliance-checker-agent non_compliant_count compliance-checker-agent redlines negotiation-advisor-agent negotiation_stance negotiation-advisor-agent

docs.title: 3. Agent Reference
docs.text:
Agent nodeID id Role Clause Extractor clause-extractor-agent w1-clause-1 Extracts and categorises contract clauses Risk Identifier risk-identifier-agent w1-risk-1 Scores each clause for risk (1–10) Compliance Checker compliance-checker-agent w1-comp-1 Checks clauses against GDPR, CCPA, Delaware law Negotiation Advisor negotiation-advisor-agent w1-nego-1 Produces redline suggestions Legal Memo legal-memo-agent w1-memo-1 Drafts the final legal memo

All agent nodes set model_name: aios:qwen3-1-7b-vllm-block. The value reaches each agent as job_data.model_name; the sample agents below ignore it and call OpenAI through the llm.py helper.

Each id is the agent's subject ID. The Delegate API looks up the running agent by this ID, so each agent must be created as a subject and deployed (so it has a runtime subject) before the workflow runs.

docs.title: 4. Step 1 — Write the Agent Code
docs.text:
Each agent is a Python class implementing two methods: on_preprocess (input validation) and on_data (core logic), and is started with main(AgentClass) from the agents SDK (core.main). All agents follow the same structure.

Each agent's job_data is the output of the previous agent plus model_name (the first agent receives the workflow input).

docs.title: 4.0 LLM Helper
docs.text:
File: llm.py — shared by all five agents.

import json
import logging
import os

from openai import OpenAI, OpenAIError

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_client: OpenAI = None


def _get_client() -> OpenAI:
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment
    return _client


def call_llm(system_prompt: str, user_message: str) -> str:
    model = os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-5.4-2026-03-05")
    client = _get_client()

    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=model,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
            {"role": "user",   "content": user_message},
        ],
        temperature=0,                            # deterministic output for structured JSON
        response_format={"type": "json_object"},  # enforce JSON mode
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content or ""


def call_llm_json(system_prompt: str, user_message: str) -> dict:
    """Calls the LLM and parses the response as JSON.

    Raises OpenAIError if the API call fails, and json.JSONDecodeError
    (a ValueError) if the response is not valid JSON.
    """
    raw_text = call_llm(system_prompt, user_message)
    clean = raw_text.strip().removeprefix("```json").removeprefix("```").removesuffix("```").strip()
    return json.loads(clean)

Never hard-code the API key in llm.py; set OPENAI_API_KEY (and optionally OPENAI_MODEL) in the agent's environment.

docs.title: 4.1 Clause Extractor Agent
docs.text:
File: clause_extractor_agent.py

Input: { "text": "<raw contract string>" } Output: { raw_contract, clauses{}, clause_count } Guards: Skips if text is missing or fewer than 20 characters.

import logging
from typing import List, Optional

from openai import OpenAIError

from core.agent_executor import AgentResult, AgentTask, Context
from core.main import main
from llm import call_llm_json

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a legal clause extraction specialist.

Given a contract text, extract and categorise every clause into the following categories:
- payment
- termination
- liability
- data_ownership
- sla
- renewal
- jurisdiction

Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object in this exact format, no preamble, no markdown:
{
  "clauses": {
    "payment":        "<verbatim or summarised clause text, or null if not found>",
    "termination":    "<verbatim or summarised clause text, or null if not found>",
    "liability":      "<verbatim or summarised clause text, or null if not found>",
    "data_ownership": "<verbatim or summarised clause text, or null if not found>",
    "sla":            "<verbatim or summarised clause text, or null if not found>",
    "renewal":        "<verbatim or summarised clause text, or null if not found>",
    "jurisdiction":   "<verbatim or summarised clause text, or null if not found>"
  },
  "clause_count": <number of non-null clauses found>
}
""".strip()


class ClauseExtractorAgent:

    def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None:
        self.subject = subject
        self.context = context

    def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask) -> Optional[List[AgentTask]]:
        text = task.job_data.get("text")
        if not text or not isinstance(text, str):
            log.warning("Task %s missing or invalid 'text' — skipping.", task.task_id)
            return None
        if len(text.strip()) < 20:
            log.warning("Task %s 'text' too short (%d chars) — skipping.", task.task_id, len(text.strip()))
            return None
        return [task]

    def get_muxer(self):
        return None

    def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult:
        try:
            raw_contract = task.job_data["text"]
            user_message = f"Extract and categorise all clauses from this contract:\n\n{raw_contract}"

            try:
                parsed = call_llm_json(SYSTEM_PROMPT, user_message)
            except OpenAIError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — OpenAI API error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"OpenAI error: {e}"})
            except ValueError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — JSON parse error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"JSON parse error: {e}"})

            clauses      = parsed.get("clauses", {})
            clause_count = parsed.get("clause_count", sum(1 for v in clauses.values() if v))

            log.info("Task %s — extracted %d clause(s)", task.task_id, clause_count)

            return AgentResult(
                task_id=task.task_id,
                job_output={"raw_contract": raw_contract, "clauses": clauses, "clause_count": clause_count},
                job_output_metadata={"clause_count": clause_count},
                is_error=False,
            )

        except Exception as e:
            log.exception("Task %s — unexpected error: %s", task.task_id, e)
            return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                               error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": str(e)})


main(ClauseExtractorAgent)

docs.title: 4.2 Risk Identifier Agent
docs.text:
File: risk_identifier_agent.py

Input: { clauses{}, raw_contract } Output: adds risks[], overall_risk_score (1–10), high_risk_count Guards: Skips if clauses is missing or all values are null.

import json
import logging
from typing import List, Optional

from openai import OpenAIError

from core.agent_executor import AgentResult, AgentTask, Context
from core.main import main
from llm import call_llm_json

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a senior legal risk analyst specialising in commercial contracts.

You will be given a set of extracted contract clauses. For each clause present,
identify any risks and assign:
- clause_type: the category of the clause
- severity: HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW
- score: integer 1-10 (10 = most dangerous)
- finding: a concise one-line description of the risk
- reasoning: 2-3 sentences explaining why this is risky

Also compute an overall_risk_score (1-10) as a weighted average across all risks.

Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object, no preamble, no markdown:
{
  "risks": [
    {
      "clause_type": "<category>",
      "severity":    "HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW",
      "score":       <1-10>,
      "finding":     "<finding>",
      "reasoning":   "<reasoning>"
    }
  ],
  "overall_risk_score": <1-10>,
  "high_risk_count":    <int>
}
""".strip()


class RiskIdentifierAgent:

    def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None:
        self.subject = subject
        self.context = context

    def get_muxer(self):
        return None

    def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask) -> Optional[List[AgentTask]]:
        clauses = task.job_data.get("clauses")
        if not clauses or not isinstance(clauses, dict):
            log.warning("Task %s missing or invalid 'clauses' — skipping.", task.task_id)
            return None
        if not {k: v for k, v in clauses.items() if v}:
            log.warning("Task %s has no non-null clauses — skipping.", task.task_id)
            return None
        return [task]

    def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult:
        try:
            clauses      = task.job_data["clauses"]
            raw_contract = task.job_data.get("raw_contract", "")
            user_message = "Identify risks in the following contract clauses:\n\n" + json.dumps(clauses, indent=2)

            try:
                parsed = call_llm_json(SYSTEM_PROMPT, user_message)
            except OpenAIError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — OpenAI API error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"OpenAI error: {e}"})
            except ValueError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — JSON parse error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"JSON parse error: {e}"})

            risks           = parsed.get("risks", [])
            overall_score   = parsed.get("overall_risk_score", 0)
            high_risk_count = parsed.get("high_risk_count", sum(1 for r in risks if r.get("severity") == "HIGH"))

            log.info("Task %s — %d risk(s), score=%s, high=%d", task.task_id, len(risks), overall_score, high_risk_count)

            return AgentResult(
                task_id=task.task_id,
                job_output={"raw_contract": raw_contract, "clauses": clauses,
                            "risks": risks, "overall_risk_score": overall_score, "high_risk_count": high_risk_count},
                job_output_metadata={"risk_count": len(risks), "overall_risk_score": overall_score,
                                     "high_risk_count": high_risk_count},
                is_error=False,
            )

        except Exception as e:
            log.exception("Task %s — unexpected error: %s", task.task_id, e)
            return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                               error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": str(e)})


main(RiskIdentifierAgent)

docs.title: 4.3 Compliance Checker Agent
docs.text:
File: compliance_checker_agent.py

Input: { risks[], clauses{}, raw_contract, overall_risk_score, high_risk_count } Output: adds compliance_findings[], non_compliant_count Guards: Skips if risks is missing or not a list.

import json
import logging
from typing import List, Optional

from openai import OpenAIError

from core.agent_executor import AgentResult, AgentTask, Context
from core.main import main
from llm import call_llm_json

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a regulatory compliance attorney specialising in GDPR, CCPA, and Delaware contract law.

You will receive a list of identified contract risks. For each risk, determine whether
the associated clause is compliant with applicable regulations.

For each finding provide:
- clause_type: the clause category
- regulation:  the specific regulation or legal standard (e.g. "GDPR Article 28", "CCPA Section 1798.100")
- status:      one of NON_COMPLIANT, AT_RISK, or COMPLIANT
- detail:      2-3 sentences explaining the compliance determination

Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object, no preamble, no markdown:
{
  "compliance_findings": [
    {
      "clause_type": "<category>",
      "regulation":  "<regulation name and section>",
      "status":      "NON_COMPLIANT|AT_RISK|COMPLIANT",
      "detail":      "<explanation>"
    }
  ],
  "non_compliant_count": <int>
}
""".strip()


class ComplianceCheckerAgent:

    def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None:
        self.subject = subject
        self.context = context

    def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask) -> Optional[List[AgentTask]]:
        risks = task.job_data.get("risks")
        if not risks or not isinstance(risks, list):
            log.warning("Task %s missing or invalid 'risks' — skipping.", task.task_id)
            return None
        return [task]

    def get_muxer(self):
        return None

    def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult:
        try:
            risks             = task.job_data["risks"]
            clauses           = task.job_data.get("clauses", {})
            raw_contract      = task.job_data.get("raw_contract", "")
            overall_score     = task.job_data.get("overall_risk_score", 0)
            high_risk_count   = task.job_data.get("high_risk_count", 0)

            user_message = ("Check the following contract risks for regulatory compliance:\n\n"
                            + json.dumps(risks, indent=2))

            try:
                parsed = call_llm_json(SYSTEM_PROMPT, user_message)
            except OpenAIError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — OpenAI API error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"OpenAI error: {e}"})
            except ValueError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — JSON parse error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"JSON parse error: {e}"})

            compliance_findings = parsed.get("compliance_findings", [])
            non_compliant_count = parsed.get("non_compliant_count",
                sum(1 for f in compliance_findings if f.get("status") == "NON_COMPLIANT"))

            log.info("Task %s — %d finding(s), %d non-compliant",
                     task.task_id, len(compliance_findings), non_compliant_count)

            return AgentResult(
                task_id=task.task_id,
                job_output={"raw_contract": raw_contract, "clauses": clauses, "risks": risks,
                            "overall_risk_score": overall_score, "high_risk_count": high_risk_count,
                            "compliance_findings": compliance_findings, "non_compliant_count": non_compliant_count},
                job_output_metadata={"compliance_findings_count": len(compliance_findings),
                                     "non_compliant_count": non_compliant_count},
                is_error=False,
            )

        except Exception as e:
            log.exception("Task %s — unexpected error: %s", task.task_id, e)
            return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                               error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": str(e)})


main(ComplianceCheckerAgent)

docs.title: 4.4 Negotiation Advisor Agent
docs.text:
File: negotiation_advisor_agent.py

Input: { risks[], compliance_findings[], clauses{}, raw_contract, overall_risk_score, high_risk_count, non_compliant_count } Output: adds redlines[], negotiation_stance Guards: Skips if either risks or compliance_findings is missing.

import json
import logging
from typing import List, Optional

from openai import OpenAIError

from core.agent_executor import AgentResult, AgentTask, Context
from core.main import main
from llm import call_llm_json

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a commercial contract negotiation specialist representing the client's interests.

You will receive identified risks and compliance findings for a contract.
For each significant issue, produce a concrete redline — a specific suggested replacement
clause that protects the client.

For each redline provide:
- clause_type:  the clause category
- priority:     HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW
- original:     the problematic language or clause summary
- suggested:    the specific replacement language to propose
- rationale:    1-2 sentences explaining how this protects the client

Also provide an overall negotiation_stance:
- REJECT:               if the contract is fundamentally unacceptable
- NEGOTIATE:            if meaningful redlines can make it acceptable
- ACCEPT_WITH_CHANGES:  if only minor tweaks are needed

Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object, no preamble, no markdown:
{
  "redlines": [
    {
      "clause_type": "<category>",
      "priority":    "HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW",
      "original":    "<problematic language>",
      "suggested":   "<replacement language>",
      "rationale":   "<rationale>"
    }
  ],
  "negotiation_stance": "REJECT|NEGOTIATE|ACCEPT_WITH_CHANGES"
}
""".strip()


class NegotiationAdvisorAgent:

    def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None:
        self.subject = subject
        self.context = context

    def get_muxer(self):
        return None

    def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask) -> Optional[List[AgentTask]]:
        if not task.job_data.get("risks") or not isinstance(task.job_data.get("risks"), list):
            log.warning("Task %s missing 'risks' — skipping.", task.task_id)
            return None
        if not task.job_data.get("compliance_findings") or not isinstance(task.job_data.get("compliance_findings"), list):
            log.warning("Task %s missing 'compliance_findings' — skipping.", task.task_id)
            return None
        return [task]

    def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult:
        try:
            risks               = task.job_data["risks"]
            compliance_findings = task.job_data["compliance_findings"]
            clauses             = task.job_data.get("clauses", {})
            raw_contract        = task.job_data.get("raw_contract", "")
            overall_score       = task.job_data.get("overall_risk_score", 0)
            high_risk_count     = task.job_data.get("high_risk_count", 0)
            non_compliant_count = task.job_data.get("non_compliant_count", 0)

            user_message = ("Produce redlines for the following risks and compliance findings:\n\n"
                            "RISKS:\n" + json.dumps(risks, indent=2)
                            + "\n\nCOMPLIANCE FINDINGS:\n" + json.dumps(compliance_findings, indent=2))

            try:
                parsed = call_llm_json(SYSTEM_PROMPT, user_message)
            except OpenAIError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — OpenAI API error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"OpenAI error: {e}"})
            except ValueError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — JSON parse error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"JSON parse error: {e}"})

            redlines           = parsed.get("redlines", [])
            negotiation_stance = parsed.get("negotiation_stance", "NEGOTIATE")

            log.info("Task %s — %d redline(s), stance=%s", task.task_id, len(redlines), negotiation_stance)

            return AgentResult(
                task_id=task.task_id,
                job_output={"raw_contract": raw_contract, "clauses": clauses, "risks": risks,
                            "overall_risk_score": overall_score, "high_risk_count": high_risk_count,
                            "compliance_findings": compliance_findings, "non_compliant_count": non_compliant_count,
                            "redlines": redlines, "negotiation_stance": negotiation_stance},
                job_output_metadata={"redline_count": len(redlines), "negotiation_stance": negotiation_stance},
                is_error=False,
            )

        except Exception as e:
            log.exception("Task %s — unexpected error: %s", task.task_id, e)
            return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                               error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": str(e)})


main(NegotiationAdvisorAgent)

docs.title: 4.5 Legal Memo Agent
docs.text:
File: legal_memo_agent.py

Input: { risks[], compliance_findings[], redlines[], clauses{}, overall_risk_score, high_risk_count, non_compliant_count, negotiation_stance } Output: { memo{}, overall_risk_score, negotiation_stance } Guards: Skips if any of risks, compliance_findings, or redlines is missing.

import json
import logging
from typing import List, Optional

from openai import OpenAIError

from core.agent_executor import AgentResult, AgentTask, Context
from core.main import main
from llm import call_llm_json

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a senior legal counsel drafting an internal memo for a client's legal team.

You will receive a full contract analysis including extracted clauses, identified risks,
compliance findings, and proposed redlines.

Produce a concise, professional legal memo with the following sections:
- executive_summary:    2-3 sentences summarising the overall situation and recommendation
- key_risks:            prose paragraph covering the most critical risks
- compliance_issues:    prose paragraph covering any regulatory compliance concerns
- recommended_redlines: prose paragraph summarising the most important redlines to push for
- recommendation:       one of REJECT, NEGOTIATE, or ACCEPT_WITH_CHANGES
- next_steps:           3-5 concrete, actionable next steps as a newline-separated list

Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object, no preamble, no markdown:
{
  "memo": {
    "executive_summary":    "<text>",
    "key_risks":            "<text>",
    "compliance_issues":    "<text>",
    "recommended_redlines": "<text>",
    "recommendation":       "REJECT|NEGOTIATE|ACCEPT_WITH_CHANGES",
    "next_steps":           "<text>"
  }
}
""".strip()


class LegalMemoAgent:

    def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None:
        self.subject = subject
        self.context = context

    def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask) -> Optional[List[AgentTask]]:
        for field in ("risks", "compliance_findings", "redlines"):
            if not task.job_data.get(field):
                log.warning("Task %s missing '%s' — skipping.", task.task_id, field)
                return None
        return [task]

    def get_muxer(self):
        return None

    def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult:
        try:
            risks               = task.job_data["risks"]
            compliance_findings = task.job_data["compliance_findings"]
            redlines            = task.job_data["redlines"]
            clauses             = task.job_data.get("clauses", {})
            overall_score       = task.job_data.get("overall_risk_score", 0)
            high_risk_count     = task.job_data.get("high_risk_count", 0)
            non_compliant_count = task.job_data.get("non_compliant_count", 0)
            negotiation_stance  = task.job_data.get("negotiation_stance", "NEGOTIATE")

            user_message = (
                "Draft a legal memo based on the following contract analysis.\n\n"
                "CLAUSES:\n"                  + json.dumps(clauses, indent=2)
                + "\n\nRISKS:\n"              + json.dumps(risks, indent=2)
                + "\n\nCOMPLIANCE FINDINGS:\n"+ json.dumps(compliance_findings, indent=2)
                + "\n\nPROPOSED REDLINES:\n"  + json.dumps(redlines, indent=2)
                + f"\n\nNEGOTIATION STANCE: {negotiation_stance}"
                + f"\nOVERALL RISK SCORE: {overall_score}/10"
                + f"\nHIGH RISK CLAUSES: {high_risk_count}"
                + f"\nNON-COMPLIANT CLAUSES: {non_compliant_count}"
            )

            try:
                parsed = call_llm_json(SYSTEM_PROMPT, user_message)
            except OpenAIError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — OpenAI API error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"OpenAI error: {e}"})
            except ValueError as e:
                log.error("Task %s — JSON parse error: %s", task.task_id, e)
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                                   error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"JSON parse error: {e}"})

            memo = parsed.get("memo", {})

            log.info("Task %s — memo generated | recommendation=%s",
                     task.task_id, memo.get("recommendation", "N/A"))

            return AgentResult(
                task_id=task.task_id,
                job_output={"memo": memo, "overall_risk_score": overall_score,
                            "negotiation_stance": negotiation_stance},
                job_output_metadata={"recommendation": memo.get("recommendation"),
                                     "overall_risk_score": overall_score},
                is_error=False,
            )

        except Exception as e:
            log.exception("Task %s — unexpected error: %s", task.task_id, e)
            return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, is_error=True,
                               error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": str(e)})


main(LegalMemoAgent)

docs.title: 5. Step 2 — Author the Workflow Spec

      "compliance-checker-agent":  ["negotiation-advisor-agent"],
      "negotiation-advisor-agent": ["legal-memo-agent"]
    }
  }
}

The workflow_uri derived from this header is:

legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable

You will need this exact string in the next step.

docs.title: 6. Step 3 — Register the Workflow
docs.text:
Register the spec with the workflow service. This stores it in the database under its workflow_uri.

curl -X POST \
  -d @./spec.json \
  http://35.223.239.192:30721/api/workflows

Check: The service returns {"success": true, "data": {...}} with the stored spec, including header.workflow_uri. Registration does not validate the spec. Problems such as duplicate nodeID values or graph references to undefined nodes appear only when the executor starts in the next step. Registering the same workflow_uri twice returns HTTP 400; use PUT /api/workflows/<workflow_uri> to replace it.

docs.title: 7. Step 4 — Deploy the Workflow Controller
docs.text:
Deploy a workflow executor that knows where to find the agents and policy engine. The deployer creates a Kubernetes Deployment and a NodePort Service (legal-contract-review-svc) in the workflows namespace.

curl -X POST \
  http://35.223.239.192:30721/api/deploy-workflow/deployer-111 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "deployment_name": "legal-contract-review",
    "workflow_id":     "legal-review-001",
    "workflow_uri":    "legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable",
    "allocation": {
      "policy_db_url":    "http://34.58.1.86:30102",
      "delegate_api_url": "http://35.223.239.192:30725"
    }
  }'

Field reference:

Field Value Notes deployment_name legal-contract-review Human-readable label workflow_id legal-review-001 Unique ID of the runtime workflow record (must not already exist) workflow_uri legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable Must match the registered spec exactly policy_db_url http://34.58.1.86:30102 Rules engine endpoint delegate_api_url http://35.223.239.192:30725 Agent execution endpoint

Response — note the url; it is the executor address used in the next step:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "id":              "legal-review-001",
    "workflow_uri":    "legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable",
    "cluster_id":      null,
    "deployer_id":     "deployer-111",
    "deployment_name": "legal-contract-review",
    "url":             "http://35.223.239.192:30712"
  }
}

Critical: The workflow_uri must be an exact match — including name, version, and release. On a mismatch the deploy call still succeeds, but the executor cannot fetch the spec at start-up (WorkflowDBError) and keeps restarting.

docs.title: 8. Step 5 — Execute a Task
docs.text:
Submit a contract for review to the executor url returned by the deploy step. Pass the raw contract text in the text field. The call is synchronous and returns when all five agents have finished.

curl -X POST \
  http://35.223.239.192:30712/api/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "text": "Contract: SaaS Subscription Agreement between Acme Corp (vendor) and RetailCo (client). Key clauses: auto-renewal at 15% price increase, no SLA guarantees, data ownership ambiguous, termination requires 180-day notice, liability cap at $5,000 regardless of contract value ($2M/year). Jurisdiction: Delaware, USA."
  }'

Input requirements:

Field Type Required Notes text string Yes Raw contract text. Must be at least 20 characters.

Note: The clause-extractor-agent is the entry node — it is the only agent that reads from text. All subsequent agents read from the structured output produced by their upstream agent.

docs.title: 9. Understanding the Output
docs.text:
The response contains the output of every node, keyed by nodeID:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "clause-extractor-agent":    { "raw_contract": "...", "clauses": { ... }, "clause_count": 6 },
    "risk-identifier-agent":     { "...": "..." },
    "compliance-checker-agent":  { "...": "..." },
    "negotiation-advisor-agent": { "...": "...", "redlines": [ ... ], "negotiation_stance": "NEGOTIATE" },
    "legal-memo-agent":          { "memo": { ... }, "overall_risk_score": 8, "negotiation_stance": "NEGOTIATE" }
  }
}

The final result is data["legal-memo-agent"]:

{
  "memo": {
    "executive_summary":    "High-level summary and overall recommendation.",
    "key_risks":            "Prose covering the most critical identified risks.",
    "compliance_issues":    "Prose covering GDPR, CCPA, or Delaware law concerns.",
    "recommended_redlines": "Prose summarising the most important clauses to renegotiate.",
    "recommendation":       "REJECT | NEGOTIATE | ACCEPT_WITH_CHANGES",
    "next_steps":           "Step 1\nStep 2\nStep 3"
  },
  "overall_risk_score": 8,
  "negotiation_stance": "NEGOTIATE"
}

Recommendation values:

Value Meaning REJECT Contract is fundamentally unacceptable — do not proceed NEGOTIATE Meaningful redlines can make it acceptable ACCEPT_WITH_CHANGES Only minor tweaks needed

docs.title: 10. Error Handling
docs.text:
All agents use the same error handling pattern:

Error Type Cause Behaviour on_preprocess returns None Required input field missing or invalid Agent is skipped — no result is produced OpenAIError LLM API call failed Returns AgentResult(is_error=True) with error details ValueError LLM response could not be parsed as JSON Returns AgentResult(is_error=True) with error details Exception Any other unexpected error Logged with full traceback, returns AgentResult(is_error=True)

What the workflow executor does with these:

  • Error result (is_error=True). The executor does not check is_error. It passes the agent's job_output — empty for an error result — to the next agent as its input.
  • Skipped agent (on_preprocess returns None). The agent sends no result back. The Delegate API waits on the session's result queue without a timeout, so the workflow executor waits too, and /api/execute does not return.

So the cascade does not end cleanly. If one agent fails, the next agent receives {"model_name": ...}, finds its required fields missing, and skips. The workflow then hangs.

Recommendation: In agents used by workflows, return an error AgentResult from on_data (or emit an error result instead of returning None from on_preprocess). Check the agent logs and the job_output of each node when debugging.

docs.title: 11. End-to-End Checklist
docs.text:
□  1. All five agents are written, created as subjects (w1-clause-1, w1-risk-1, w1-comp-1,
       w1-nego-1, w1-memo-1) and deployed, with OPENAI_API_KEY set in their environment
□  2. spec.json is saved with the correct header and graph
□  3. Workflow registered:
       curl -X POST -d @./spec.json http://35.223.239.192:30721/api/workflows
□  4. Executor deployed:
       curl -X POST http://35.223.239.192:30721/api/deploy-workflow/deployer-111 ...
       workflow_uri = "legal-contract-review-pipeline-1:1.0.0-stable"
       note data.url from the response
□  5. Task submitted:
       curl -X POST <data.url>/api/execute ...
       body = { "text": "<contract text>" }
□  6. Output reviewed — check data["legal-memo-agent"].memo.recommendation and overall_risk_score
